notes: Gold labels checked by the orchestrator. Real cases come from this repository's history: defects our reviewers flagged and the next round fixed, or that the orchestrator caught after all gates passed. Required defects count toward recall; optional ones (genuine but low impact) are neither required nor false positives. Clean cases are merged heads with no later fix; grade them on false blocks (request_changes or any blocker/major finding). A finding matches a defect when it names the same file and a line within the range ±5 (file-level findings with line 0 match on file alone only for completeness defects). v1.1 (2026-09-26): review-013/014/015 were labelled clean but the first sweep found real defects in them (verified ones required, others optional); the clean set is now the three small sandbox diffs and needs more genuinely clean cases. v2 (2026-09-28, issue #115): review-016..031 are escaped defects (approved heads whose defects were found later by orchestrator review agents, production or the review eval); review-032..039 are merged PRs with no known defect. Severity maps high/medium/low to blocker/major/minor; required = high and medium. review-014's two Discord defects are now required (confirmed by failing tests in PR #19). Cases whose base..head history contains evals/* carry snapshot: true and need the sanitized-snapshot mode. v2 excludes cases whose only defects are low severity (every defect optional): under verdict-based pass grading they would reward blocking on a minor finding. Re-add them once the grader supports detection-only cases.

input.prompt:
GitHub webhook trigger

Add a GitHub webhook integration so runs can be triggered from GitHub.

- New module `src/integrations/github.ts`, mounted from `src/integrations/index.ts` as route
  `POST /webhooks/github`.
- Verify `X-Hub-Signature-256` (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` from
  `cfg.secrets`) using a constant-time comparison; reject with 401 when missing/invalid. If the
  secret is not configured, the route responds 503 and startup notes say webhooks are disabled.
- Deduplicate deliveries by `X-GitHub-Delivery` using `store.recordInbox` (ignore repeats with 200).
  Record every delivery in the inbox with its outcome (`ignored`, `run_created`, `error`) and a note.
- Only act for the owner configured as `cfg.githubOwner` (and `dependabot[bot]` for Dependabot PRs).
  Everything else is recorded as `ignored`. Issue/PR text is untrusted: quote it into the run
  prompt as data, never as instructions.
- Triggers:
  - `issues` with action `labeled` and label `limitless` → run with the issue title + body as the
    prompt, `sourceRef` {kind:"issue", repo, number}.
  - `issue_comment` `created` whose body starts with `/limitless ` by the owner → run with the text
    after the command plus the issue context.
  - `pull_request` `opened`/`reopened`/`synchronize` by `dependabot[bot]` → a `quick` profile run
    whose prompt asks to verify the dependency update (run gates, fix breakages caused by the bump),
    with the run's base branch set to the PR's head branch so the fix lands on Dependabot's branch.
    If that needs engine support (base branch = PR head, deliver by pushing to that branch and
    commenting instead of opening a new PR), add it cleanly.
- Report back on GitHub with the `gh` CLI (factory context, not agents): comment on the
  issue/PR when a run is created (with run id) and when it finishes (status, PR link, cost). Use a
  small notifier that subscribes to store run updates and only reacts to runs with a GitHub
  `sourceRef`.
- Tests: signature verification (valid/invalid/missing), dedupe, owner filtering, each trigger
  mapping to the right CreateRunRequest, and that untrusted text is quoted. Use recorded sample
  payloads; never call GitHub in tests (inject the `gh` runner).
- Document setup in README (webhook URL `https://limitless.mattflower.cc/webhooks/github`, content
  type JSON, secret, events: Issues, Issue comments, Pull requests).

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add an authenticated GitHub webhook that turns selected owner actions and Dependabot pull requests into Limitless runs. Use the existing inbox for delivery deduplication and audit outcomes, and post run updates through a factory-side GitHub notifier. Extend the pipeline’s branch and delivery path so Dependabot fixes can land on the existing pull request.
assumptions: For labeled issues, both the issue author and the actor applying the label must match cfg.githubOwner. For command comments, the commenter must match cfg.githubOwner.
Dependabot runs require a pull request authored by dependabot[bot], an allowed event actor, and a head branch in the same repository as the pull request base.
An authenticated request without X-GitHub-Delivery or with malformed JSON receives 400. Requests that fail authentication are not recorded in the inbox.
Duplicate delivery IDs receive 200 without creating another run or posting another creation comment. A processing failure is recorded as error and reported with a server error.
Comment failures are logged without changing the run outcome.
requirements: Add src/integrations/github.ts and mount POST /webhooks/github through src/integrations/index.ts. Include an enabled or disabled startup note and unsubscribe the notifier during integration shutdown.

When cfg.secrets.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent, return 503. Otherwise verify X-Hub-Signature-256 against an HMAC-SHA256 computed from the unmodified request body bytes, using a constant-time digest comparison; return 401 for missing or invalid signatures.

Atomically claim each authenticated delivery ID with store.recordInbox before creating a run. Extend the store API as needed to finalize the existing inbox row with status ignored, run_created, or error, plus a note and run ID when applicable. Record unsupported events and filtered actors as ignored.

Validate event shape and repository identity before mapping it to CreateRunRequest. Use the payload repository’s canonical full name, source github, and a sourceRef identifying issue or pull request, repository, and number.

Map an owner’s issues.labeled event for the limitless label to a run whose prompt includes the issue title and body. Map an owner’s issue_comment.created event beginning with /limitless followed by text to a run whose prompt includes that text and issue context. Put all issue and comment content in clearly delimited, escaped quoted data sections.

Map pull_request.opened, reopened, and synchronize events for eligible Dependabot pull requests to profile quick. The prompt must ask for dependency update verification, gates, and fixes caused by the bump; quote pull request text as untrusted data.

Extend CreateRunRequest, persistence, prepare, and delivery so a Dependabot run starts from the pull request head branch, works in its own worktree branch, and pushes a verified fast-forward result to that existing head branch. Do not create or merge a new pull request; refuse delivery if the remote head moved or the pull request comes from a fork.

Add a small notifier subscribed to store run events. For GitHub sourceRefs, use an injectable gh runner to comment on the source issue or pull request when a run is created and when it reaches a terminal status. The final comment includes status, any PR link, and cost. Prevent repeated comments from routine updates to the same run state.

Add recorded sample payload tests for authentication, deduplication, filtering, trigger mapping, quoted untrusted text, inbox outcomes, notifier behavior, and Dependabot branch delivery. Tests must use fakes for paid models and gh and make no network calls. Document the webhook URL, JSON content type, secret, and Issues, Issue comments, and Pull requests events in README.

Changing repository-wide merge policy for ordinary runs.

defects.summary: Existing-branch delivery (skip PR, force-push to run.deliveryBranch) is authorized by the mere presence of deliveryBranch; nothing requires the run to come from the signature-verified GitHub/Dependabot webhook. deliveryBranch/baseBranch/sourceRef are accepted verbatim from POST /api/runs (store.ts createRun), so any API caller could get a run force-pushed onto main, bypassing mergePolicy and PR review.

input.prompt:
Blind holdout scenarios

Add StrongDM-style holdout checks that the implementer never sees (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3).

- New stage `holdout` for `standard`/`deep` profiles: after `spec`, a separate invocation (role
  `holdout`, read-only, different vendor than the spec author when possible) writes 3–8 concrete
  scenarios from the original request + spec only: each with id `H-n`, a description, exact steps
  (commands to run / inputs) and the expected observable outcome, including at least two edge or
  failure cases not literally listed in the acceptance criteria. Zod schema + strict JSON schema.
- Start it concurrently with the first implement round (it must not delay implementation); await it
  before verify. Store scenarios in run state and as an artifact that is only written after
  delivery (the implementer must not be able to read them from disk during the run).
- `verify` receives both the acceptance criteria and the holdout scenarios, reports each `H-n` with
  met/unmet/unclear + evidence. Unmet holdout scenarios produce implementer feedback that describes
  the *observed failure* without revealing the scenario text verbatim.
- PR report gets a "Holdout scenarios" table.
- Tests with the fake harness: holdout runs in parallel with implement, verify prompt contains the
  scenarios, feedback for an unmet scenario does not contain the scenario's steps, resume after a
  restart doesn't lose the scenarios.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add blind holdout scenarios to standard and deep runs so an independent author can test behavior beyond the published acceptance criteria. The author starts alongside the first implementation round, and the verifier judges both sets of checks before delivery. Scenarios remain in persisted run state until delivery makes them available as an artifact and in the PR report.
assumptions: Quick runs continue without a holdout stage.
A same-vendor holdout author is acceptable when routing has no available author from another vendor; record that fallback.
The existing runs.state_json can persist scenarios and generation status without a new migration. A migration is required only if implementation adds database columns.
If holdout generation fails after the configured routing attempts, the run cannot pass verification and needs human attention.
requirements: Add a holdout author prompt and Zod schema, passed through toStrictJsonSchema, for 3–8 scenarios with unique sequential H-n IDs, a description, exact executable steps or inputs, and an expected observable outcome. Require at least two edge or failure cases not literally listed in the spec's acceptance criteria.

For standard and deep profiles, start one read-only holdout invocation after spec and concurrently with the first implement round. Supply only the original request and completed spec; prevent access to the changing implementation worktree. Prefer a vendor different from the spec author's and record the selected model.

Keep implementation independent of holdout completion. Await holdout results before verify, including when earlier rounds fail gates or review. Coordinate concurrent stage bookkeeping without losing either stage's status or corrupting the run's current stage.
Persist validated scenarios and enough generation status in run state to survive restart. Resume must reuse completed scenarios or safely retry interrupted generation without duplicate scenario sets.

Do not put scenario text or steps in the implementer's prompt, feedback, worktree, pre-delivery artifacts, or accessible event logs. Publish a dedicated scenarios artifact only after delivery; keep failed or cancelled runs from leaking it prematurely.

Extend verify input and structured result to report each AC-n and H-n as met, unmet, or unclear with evidence. The engine must treat missing, unclear, or unmet entries as failure regardless of the verifier's overall claim.

For failed holdouts, give the next implement round the observed failure and evidence in paraphrased form without copying the scenario description, steps, or expected outcome. Add a Holdout scenarios table with per-scenario result and evidence to the delivery report.
Use the fake harness for pipeline and restart tests; no tests may call a real model, network, or gh. Run bun run check before completion.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A standard or deep run starts exactly one read-only holdout author after spec, while the first implement invocation can proceed before the author finishes; a quick run starts none.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add fake-harness pipeline tests that block holdout completion until implement begins, inspect invocation roles and modes, and compare quick, standard, and deep runs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Holdout output validates as 3–8 uniquely identified H-n scenarios with descriptions, exact steps, expected outcomes, and two additional edge or failure cases; invalid structured output follows the existing fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add schema tests for valid, too-short, too-long, duplicate-ID, missing-field, and invalid-output cases; run bun test.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The holdout author sees only the original request and spec, uses a vendor different from the spec author when available, and cannot inspect implementation changes made during its invocation.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: In a fake-harness test, inspect the holdout prompt and cwd while implement edits the worktree, then inspect recorded model vendors and the same-vendor fallback case.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: After a restart, completed holdout scenarios remain available to verify without authoring a second set; an interrupted holdout is retried or resolved before verify.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a fake-harness restart test that stops and recreates the Factory between holdout generation and verification, then checks persisted run state, invocation counts, and verify input.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Verify receives every acceptance criterion and holdout scenario, records a status and evidence for each, and fails the round if any required entry is missing, unmet, or unclear.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add fake-harness tests that inspect the verify prompt and return an erroneous overall pass with one missing or unmet H-n; assert the engine rejects the round.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An unmet holdout produces actionable implementer feedback about the observed failure without exposing the scenario's exact steps, description, or expected outcome.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use a distinctive secret marker in fake holdout steps and inspect the next implement prompt, feedback state, and pre-delivery artifacts for its absence while checking that failure evidence is present.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Before delivery, no scenarios artifact or implementation-readable scenario file exists; after delivery, the scenarios artifact and the PR report's Holdout scenarios table include all H-n results and evidence.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add fake-harness assertions before and after delivery using Store.listArtifacts/getArtifact, worktree file inspection, and renderReport output.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The repository passes lint, type checking, and tests with the new pipeline behavior.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run bun run check.

out_of_scope: Changing the deterministic gates, diff audit, or review policy beyond integrating holdout results into verification and reporting.
Adding holdouts to the quick profile.
Letting an LLM choose pipeline control flow or implementation rounds.

input.prompt:
Blind holdout scenarios

Add StrongDM-style holdout checks that the implementer never sees (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3).

- New stage `holdout` for `standard`/`deep` profiles: after `spec`, a separate invocation (role
  `holdout`, read-only, different vendor than the spec author when possible) writes 3–8 concrete
  scenarios from the original request + spec only: each with id `H-n`, a description, exact steps
  (commands to run / inputs) and the expected observable outcome, including at least two edge or
  failure cases not literally listed in the acceptance criteria. Zod schema + strict JSON schema.
- Start it concurrently with the first implement round (it must not delay implementation); await it
  before verify. Store scenarios in run state and as an artifact that is only written after
  delivery (the implementer must not be able to read them from disk during the run).
- `verify` receives both the acceptance criteria and the holdout scenarios, reports each `H-n` with
  met/unmet/unclear + evidence. Unmet holdout scenarios produce implementer feedback that describes
  the *observed failure* without revealing the scenario text verbatim.
- PR report gets a "Holdout scenarios" table.
- Tests with the fake harness: holdout runs in parallel with implement, verify prompt contains the
  scenarios, feedback for an unmet scenario does not contain the scenario's steps, resume after a
  restart doesn't lose the scenarios.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add blind holdout scenarios to standard and deep runs so an independent author can test behavior beyond the published acceptance criteria. The author starts alongside the first implementation round, and the verifier judges both sets of checks before delivery. Scenarios remain in persisted run state until delivery makes them available as an artifact and in the PR report.
assumptions: Quick runs continue without a holdout stage.
A same-vendor holdout author is acceptable when routing has no available author from another vendor; record that fallback.
The existing runs.state_json can persist scenarios and generation status without a new migration. A migration is required only if implementation adds database columns.
If holdout generation fails after the configured routing attempts, the run cannot pass verification and needs human attention.
requirements: Add a holdout author prompt and Zod schema, passed through toStrictJsonSchema, for 3–8 scenarios with unique sequential H-n IDs, a description, exact executable steps or inputs, and an expected observable outcome. Require at least two edge or failure cases not literally listed in the spec's acceptance criteria.

For standard and deep profiles, start one read-only holdout invocation after spec and concurrently with the first implement round. Supply only the original request and completed spec; prevent access to the changing implementation worktree. Prefer a vendor different from the spec author's and record the selected model.

Keep implementation independent of holdout completion. Await holdout results before verify, including when earlier rounds fail gates or review. Coordinate concurrent stage bookkeeping without losing either stage's status or corrupting the run's current stage.
Persist validated scenarios and enough generation status in run state to survive restart. Resume must reuse completed scenarios or safely retry interrupted generation without duplicate scenario sets.

Do not put scenario text or steps in the implementer's prompt, feedback, worktree, pre-delivery artifacts, or accessible event logs. Publish a dedicated scenarios artifact only after delivery; keep failed or cancelled runs from leaking it prematurely.

Extend verify input and structured result to report each AC-n and H-n as met, unmet, or unclear with evidence. The engine must treat missing, unclear, or unmet entries as failure regardless of the verifier's overall claim.

For failed holdouts, give the next implement round the observed failure and evidence in paraphrased form without copying the scenario description, steps, or expected outcome. Add a Holdout scenarios table with per-scenario result and evidence to the delivery report.
Use the fake harness for pipeline and restart tests; no tests may call a real model, network, or gh. Run bun run check before completion.

input.prompt:
Quota alerts

Tell the operator when a subscription reaches its reserve, so banked resets can be applied in time.

- When a provider transitions into `exhausted` (quota reserve reached, or a hard limit hit), or
  crosses 75% of its reserve for the first time in a window, emit one alert per provider per window:
  a Discord message in the configured channel (when Discord is enabled) and a banner on the UI
  dashboard (a new `alerts` field on `/api/providers` or a small `/api/alerts` endpoint).
- Include the provider, which window, utilization, when it resets, and what the router will do
  meanwhile (which providers it falls back to).
- Tests with a fake Discord port and a fake clock: one alert per window, no alert storms on
  flapping, reset clears it.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add quota alerts so the operator can apply banked resets before a subscription becomes unavailable. The provider tracker will create a durable alert when a quota window first reaches 75% of its configured reserve or the provider becomes exhausted. The dashboard will show the alert, and the existing Discord integration will send it to the configured channel when enabled.
assumptions: 75% of reserve means utilization >= 0.75 × that window’s configured reserve, not 75% of the provider’s hard quota.
The first observation above the threshold counts as a crossing when no earlier observation exists for that window.
A warning and later exhaustion in the same provider window produce one Discord message; the dashboard may update that alert to show the current exhausted state.

Fallback providers depend on routing role and constraints. Alert text will describe that the router skips an exhausted provider and list currently eligible alternatives without promising a universal order.
If a hard limit has no named quota window, use a clearly labeled hard-limit alert and the best available reset estimate; show an unknown reset time when none is available.
requirements: Detect threshold crossings from quota telemetry in ProviderTracker and exhausted transitions caused by either reserve utilization or a quota rejection. Do not treat health failures, circuit breakers, or metered budget exhaustion as subscription quota alerts.

Identify alerts by provider, quota window, and window reset boundary. Persist alert and deduplication state through a new numbered migration so daemon restarts and repeated telemetry cannot resend an alert for the same window.
Rearm a provider-window alert only when that window resets or telemetry identifies a new reset boundary. Expired windows must not keep an alert active.

Expose current alerts through a small /api/alerts endpoint and deliver changes to the dashboard using the existing live update mechanism. Render a visible dashboard banner with provider, window, utilization, reset time, severity, and routing behavior.
When Discord is enabled, send each new alert once to discordChannelId through DiscordPort. Discord being disabled or a send failure must not block quota tracking, routing, or dashboard display.

Build fallback information from current router and provider state. For a warning, say whether the provider remains eligible; for exhaustion, say it is skipped and identify eligible fallback providers or state that none are available.
Keep alert generation deterministic and testable with an injected clock and fake Discord port; do not call paid models, the network, or gh in tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: For each configured subscription window, the first observed utilization at or above 75% of its reserve creates one alert containing the provider, window, utilization, reset time, and routing behavior.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a fake-clock tracker test that observes values below, at, and above 0.75 × the configured reserve, then inspects /api/alerts or the alert store.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Reaching a reserve or receiving a quota rejection creates an exhausted alert even when no earlier warning was observed; health and circuit-breaker transitions do not.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add tracker tests for reserve exhaustion, record(provider, 'quota'), and record(provider, 'unavailable'), asserting the resulting alert set.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Repeated observations, quota-result flapping, and a warning followed by exhaustion send at most one Discord message for the same provider and window, including across a daemon restart.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use the existing fake DiscordPort with a temporary SQLite store; replay those transitions, recreate the tracker and integration, and assert one post to the configured channel.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: After a window resets, its prior alert clears and a threshold crossing in the next window can create a new alert.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Advance the fake clock past resetsAt, inspect /api/alerts, then observe telemetry with a new reset boundary and assert one new alert and Discord post.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The dashboard displays current alerts on initial load and reflects alert creation, exhaustion updates, and clearing without a manual reload.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add an API and live-update test, then inspect the dashboard with seeded provider telemetry and alert transitions.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Alerts identify only currently eligible fallback providers, report when none exist, and remain available in the UI when Discord is disabled or sending fails.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use fake router/provider states and a failing or disabled fake Discord port; assert alert content and continued API availability.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Lint, type checking, and the full test suite pass.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run bun run check.

out_of_scope: Automatically applying banked resets or changing provider quota limits.
Changing routing policy or allowing an LLM to decide alert or fallback behavior.
Adding notification channels other than the existing Discord integration and dashboard.

input.prompt:
Rebase before delivery

When the base branch moved while a run was working, deliver should rebase instead of opening a PR
that conflicts.

- In `deliver`, fetch the base branch; if it advanced past `run.baseSha`, rebase the run branch onto
  it. On a clean rebase, re-run the gates (not review/verify) and only deliver if nothing regressed;
  update `baseSha`.
- On conflicts: abort the rebase and run one extra implement round whose feedback tells the agent to
  merge the new base (`git merge origin/<base>`), resolve conflicts preserving both intents, and
  re-run checks; then continue through gates/audit/review as usual.
- Tests with local git repos: base advanced without conflict (rebased, gates re-run), with conflict
  (extra round), base unchanged (no-op).

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass. `bun run smoke` exercises the real agent CLIs if you change harness code (optional, spends a little quota).

spec.summary: Before delivering a new GitHub branch, Limitless will fetch its base branch and check whether it advanced since the run’s recorded `baseSha`. A clean rebase will trigger another gate run before delivery; a conflicting rebase will be aborted and sent through one additional implement round with merge-resolution feedback. This prevents delivery of a branch known to conflict with its base.
assumptions: This applies to new GitHub PR delivery. Existing PR-head updates keep their current webhook-head and guarded-push behavior.
Tests use local bare Git repositories as remotes, the fake harness, and no network or `gh` calls.
A gate regression after a clean rebase blocks delivery; it does not trigger another review or verify.
requirements: At successful delivery, fetch the configured base branch and compare its fetched tip with `run.baseSha`. If unchanged, continue the existing delivery path.
If the fetched tip descends from `run.baseSha`, rebase the committed run branch onto that exact tip. Do not publish while a rebase is in progress.

After a clean rebase, rerun the configured setup and gates, persist their results, and block delivery if a previously passing check now fails or setup prevents checks from running. Do not rerun audit, review, or verify solely because the rebase was clean.
After successful post-rebase gates, persist the new `baseSha` and rebased `headSha` before building the delivery report and publishing.

If rebase conflicts, abort it and verify the worktree is out of rebase state. Give the implementer one additional round, even if the normal round budget was exhausted, with feedback directing it to merge `origin/<base>`, resolve conflicts while preserving both intents, and rerun checks.
Run the conflict-resolution round through the existing gates, diff audit, and review flow, plus verify where the run profile requires it. Use the new base SHA for subsequent diffs and delivery.

Persist enough phase and round state for a restart to resume the appropriate post-rebase gate check or conflict-resolution round without publishing an unchecked branch. If the base changes again before publication, fail closed or repeat the base check.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When the base advances without conflicting with run commits, the delivered head contains the new base commit, `baseSha` records that commit, and gates run again while review and verify invocation counts remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a fake-harness pipeline test with a local bare Git remote that advances the base after review; run `bun test test/pipeline.test.ts` and inspect commit ancestry, stored SHAs, stage records, and invocation counts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When the fetched base equals `run.baseSha`, delivery makes no rebase commit and adds no gate, review, verify, or implement round.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add an unchanged-base case to `test/pipeline.test.ts`; run `bun test test/pipeline.test.ts` and compare the delivered head and stage counts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When rebase conflicts, Git rebase is aborted, no branch is published in the conflicted state, and exactly one additional implement invocation receives the merge-and-resolve instruction.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a conflicting-base case using a local bare Git remote and fake harness; run `bun test test/pipeline.test.ts`, inspect the second implement prompt, Git rebase state, and remote refs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: After the conflict-resolution implement round, delivery occurs only after the normal gates, audit, review, and profile-required verify stages pass against the updated base.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: In the conflict test, have the fake implementer complete the merge, then assert stage order, updated-base diff behavior, and delivered ancestry with `bun test test/pipeline.test.ts`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: If a clean rebase causes a gate or setup regression, no push or PR creation occurs and the run records the failed check.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a base-advance fixture that makes a formerly passing gate fail after rebase; run `bun test test/pipeline.test.ts` and inspect gate results and unchanged remote refs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Existing PR-head delivery still rejects a remote head that moved beyond its verified webhook SHA.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun test test/github-delivery.test.ts test/pipeline.test.ts`, including the existing concurrent-head update case.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Lint, type checking, and the full test suite pass in a writable test environment.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun run check`.

out_of_scope: Changing harness adapters or invoking real agent CLIs.
Automatically merging a delivered PR or changing merge policy.
Rewriting shipped database migrations.

defects.summary: fetchBase runs 'git fetch origin refs/heads/B:refs/remotes/origin/B' in the worktree (shared object store/refs of the bare cache) without withRepoLock; concurrent runs on the same repo race on the ref lock and delivery fails intermittently ('cannot lock ref'). Called up to 3x per delivery without allowFail.

fetchBase's refspec has no leading '+', so a force-pushed/rewritten base branch makes git reject the non-fast-forward update and sh() throws a raw git error before the isAncestor guard can report 'base branch no longer descends from the recorded base'. Carried over: also present in this head, first flagged in review round 1; 7ee37e75 rewrote this function for the race but kept the non-'+' refspec; fixed in faf8e2ca.

When the base advances and the rebase conflicts, deliver() updates run.baseSha and sends the implementer back to 'git merge origin/<base>', but ctx.state.baselineScripts (captured once in prepare from the original base) is never refreshed; the re-run audit compares old-base scripts against the merged package.json and raises a block-severity gate-script-changed finding for upstream script changes. Reviewer cited src/gates/audit.ts:202 (the rule); the fix landed in engine.ts. Carried over: present in this head, first flagged in review round 1; fixed in faf8e2ca.

input.prompt:
Chat concierge

A conversational front door shared by the UI `/chat` page and Discord free-text mentions.

- `src/concierge.ts`: given a conversation (stored in `chat_messages`), a cheap model (role `chat`)
  returns a structured action: `reply` (text), `propose_run` (repo, prompt, profile, title — shown
  for confirmation), `create_run` (only after the user confirmed a proposal), `status` (run id or
  "recent"), `answer_question` (run id, answer). The daemon executes actions; the model never calls
  APIs directly. Include known repos and recent runs in the context.
- API: `POST /api/chat/:conversationId/messages`, `GET /api/chat/:conversationId`; SSE updates.
- UI: the `/chat` page with a message list, proposal cards with Confirm/Edit buttons, and links to
  created runs.
- Tests with the fake harness for each action type and for confirmation being required before a run
  is created.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass. `bun run smoke` exercises the real agent CLIs if you change harness code (optional, spends a little quota).

spec.summary: Build a shared chat concierge for the SolidJS `/chat` page and authorized Discord mentions. It will use the existing `chat` model routing policy to interpret conversations into validated actions, while daemon code handles status queries, answers, and run creation. Persisted proposals and explicit confirmation will ensure that conversational requests cannot silently start runs.
assumptions: UI and Discord share the concierge service and action semantics; they do not automatically share conversation histories.
Conversations are created lazily on the first message. The UI retains its conversation identifier across reloads; Discord identifiers are scoped to the configured guild, channel or thread, and owner.
The default proposal profile is `auto`; supported profiles remain `auto`, `quick`, `standard`, and `deep`.
Discord confirmation uses an explicit `confirm <proposal-id>` mention. General affirmative text is not sufficient authorization.
The `recent` status target returns at most 15 runs, matching the existing Discord recent-runs limit.
An `answer_question` action answers all currently open questions on the specified run, matching the existing `Factory.answer` behavior.
requirements: Implement `src/concierge.ts` as a daemon-owned service shared through Factory by HTTP and Discord. Reuse the existing Router, ProviderTracker, injectable harnesses, Store, and Factory operations; do not create synthetic runs or pipeline stages merely to process chat.

Define shared chat message, proposal, action, and stream types in `src/core/types.ts`. Validate model output at runtime using Zod and provider-compatible structured JSON schema. Support exactly `reply` with text, `propose_run` with repo/prompt/profile/title, `create_run` referencing a stored proposal, `status` targeting a run ID or `recent`, and `answer_question` with run ID and answer.

Invoke models through role `chat` using the existing routing policy, readonly mode, and `noTools`. Respect provider availability, concurrency, quota telemetry, and bounded failure handling. Model output must never directly invoke APIs, tools, or arbitrary daemon methods.

Build each model prompt from persisted conversation history, known repository identifiers, recent run summaries, and the current proposal state. Bound model context without deleting stored history. Treat conversation and repository/run text as data; confirmation authority must come from validated user input rather than model assertions.

Add Store methods for ordered chat history and structured action outcomes using the existing `chat_messages` table. Persist proposal identity, contents, lifecycle state, confirmation, and resulting run linkage. Any schema additions must use a new numbered migration without changing shipped migrations. Publish typed chat updates through Store subscriptions.

Enforce confirmation in deterministic code. A proposal creates no run. Confirmation must identify the current pending proposal in the same conversation, and creation must use its exact stored repo, prompt, profile, and title. Reject missing, foreign, superseded, or unconfirmed proposals and model attempts to alter confirmed values. Edits produce a new pending proposal requiring fresh confirmation.

Serialize processing within each conversation and durably associate each consumed proposal with its created run. Duplicate or concurrent confirmation and replay after reopening the Store must not create a second run. Confirmation may execute the validated `create_run` action directly without another model call.

Execute run creation through the existing Factory creation path and repository resolution rules. Record UI concierge runs with source `chat` and Discord runs with source `discord`, retaining conversation and requester provenance. Query Store for authoritative status responses and use `Factory.answer` for nonblank answers; unknown runs and runs without open questions return useful errors without unrelated mutations.

Add `POST /api/chat/:conversationId/messages` for a validated text, confirmation, or edit submission, and `GET /api/chat/:conversationId` for ordered history and proposal/run state. Define a typed request union that distinguishes these submissions and references proposal IDs explicitly. Reject blank messages, malformed JSON, invalid profiles, and invalid proposal transitions. A valid unused conversation ID returns empty history. Apply existing HTTP origin, JSON content-type, and tunnel restrictions.

Add conversation-scoped SSE, following the existing `/api/runs/:id/stream` pattern, with persisted message IDs and an `after` cursor for replay. Stream committed user/assistant messages, proposal changes, errors, and created-run links. Reconnection must recover missed outcomes without duplicate visible messages or updates from another conversation; unsubscribe on disconnect.

Replace `ui/pages/Chat.tsx` with a message list and composer using `ui/api.ts` conventions. Render proposals with repo, prompt, profile, title, Confirm, and Edit controls. Editing must visibly present the revised proposal before confirmation. Show pending/error states, disable invalid or consumed confirmation controls, reconcile POST and SSE results, restore history after reload, and link created runs to `/runs/:id`.

Extend DiscordPort message metadata to identify actual bot mentions and message IDs. Route only nonbot messages from the configured owner in the configured channel or recognized run threads to the concierge when explicitly mentioned. Display complete proposal details and confirmation instructions, splitting messages when needed. Preserve existing slash commands and unmentioned run-thread answers; mentioned messages must not also be recorded as question answers. Reuse run-thread creation and progress behavior for confirmed Discord runs.

Add deterministic tests using `src/harness/fake.ts`, injected dependencies, and the existing fake DiscordPort pattern. Cover all actions, confirmation enforcement, persistence, HTTP/SSE behavior, and failure paths without real models, external network access, or `gh`. The implementation must pass `bun run check` and `bun run build:ui`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The shared concierge routes through role `chat`, requests structured output with tools disabled, and executes each of the five supported action types through deterministic daemon handlers.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add `test/concierge.test.ts` using fakeHarness replies for every action. Inspect captured AgentSpec values and prompt context, assert resulting messages and Factory calls, and verify ordinary replies and status requests create no runs. Run `bun test test/concierge.test.ts`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Only explicit confirmation of the exact current proposal creates a run, and each proposal creates at most one run.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add tests for unsolicited model `create_run`, fabricated confirmation claims, wrong-conversation IDs, edited or superseded proposals, changed creation fields, duplicate/concurrent confirmation, and confirmation replay after reopening the Store. Assert zero creations for unauthorized attempts and one creation with the exact stored fields for valid confirmation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Conversation history, proposal state, and created-run links persist and remain isolated between conversations; API requests are validated and protected by existing HTTP restrictions.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add `test/chat-http.test.ts` invoking createHttpRoutes handlers with constructed Requests and a fake-backed Factory. Test empty history, text/edit/confirm submissions, Store reopen, conversation separation, malformed or blank input, invalid profiles, foreign Origin, incorrect content type, and tunnel headers. Run `bun test test/chat-http.test.ts`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SSE delivers committed updates only for the requested conversation and supports replay without duplicate visible messages.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: In chat HTTP tests, consume the returned stream using a stub server, post messages and proposal transitions, then reconnect with an `after` cursor. Assert ordered persisted IDs, recovery of missed updates, absence of another conversation's messages, client deduplication, and subscription cleanup on abort.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Status and answer actions use actual stored runs and questions, and invalid model output or unavailable models never cause unintended mutations.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add fake-harness cases for a specific run, recent and empty run lists, unknown run IDs, multiple open questions, no open questions, blank answers, malformed/unknown actions, and exhausted routing candidates. Assert authoritative results, useful failure messages, bounded attempts, and unchanged run/question state on failures.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Authorized Discord mentions use the same persisted concierge and confirmation rules while existing commands and unmentioned thread answers continue to work.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Extend `test/discord.test.ts` with fake-port mention, proposal, edit, explicit confirmation, duplicate delivery, and created-run/thread cases. Assert bots, nonowners, and unrelated channels trigger no concierge call; mentioned status requests do not answer questions. Run `bun test test/discord.test.ts`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The `/chat` page supports a complete message-to-proposal-to-confirmed-run flow, including edits, reloads, pending states, and recoverable errors.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use a locally seeded fake-harness daemon with the scheduler disabled. Send a request, inspect proposal fields, edit and reconfirm, verify exactly one linked run, reload to restore history, and simulate a failed response and SSE reconnect. Confirm controls cannot submit an obsolete or consumed proposal.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The implementation conforms to repository checks and builds the SolidJS UI without requiring paid services.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun run check` and `bun run build:ui`; both must exit successfully. Inspect new tests to confirm harness, Discord, and external delivery dependencies are fake or stubbed.

out_of_scope: Changes to pipeline stage selection, scheduling policy, delivery policy, or model-decided orchestration.
New chat actions for cancellation, retry, deployment, merge, or arbitrary API/tool execution.
Multiuser authentication, Discord direct messages, or automatic synchronization of UI and Discord conversations.
Conversation search, attachments, voice input, transcript deletion, or a conversation-management interface.
A general harness rewrite or a new model provider.
Real-agent smoke runs as a required test; `bun run smoke` remains optional and quota-consuming.

Direct-HTTP LLM path + local model servers

- `src/harness/llm.ts`: single structured completions over OpenAI-compatible HTTP
  (`/v1/chat/completions` with `response_format: json_schema`, falling back to extract-and-validate
  with one retry) for providers with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (mtplx, twilight llama.cpp,

  (unit file generated by the command; model path configurable).
- Tests with a local fake OpenAI-compatible server (Bun.serve in the test).

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). spec.summary: Add a direct HTTP harness for single structured completions from mtplx, twilight, and OpenRouter, and route tool-free roles through it to avoid Claude Code's prompt overhead. Add CLI commands to manage the Mac mtplx server and twilight llama-server, with local fake-server tests for the HTTP path.
assumptions: The existing `baseUrl` remains the Anthropic-compatible URL used by agentic Claude CLI calls; `openaiBaseUrl` is a separate provider field for direct HTTP calls.
Triage is the currently implemented tool-free role. Chat and summarize should use this path when their invocation flows are implemented.
The new local commands manage the existing mtplx launchd agent and a generated twilight systemd user unit, without requiring either server during tests.
A configured twilight model path identifies an already installed model; downloading models is outside this task.
requirements: Add `src/harness/llm.ts` using the existing `Harness` and `AgentResult` contracts. Send one non-streaming request to the selected provider's `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with its model, prompt, optional system text, bearer token, and `response_format: { type: "json_schema", ... }`.

Validate the returned content against the requested schema. If structured output is unsupported or the response is invalid, extract a JSON object from the text and validate it; make at most one corrective retry before returning a structured failure.

Honor cancellation and invocation timeout. Classify HTTP, transport, and malformed-response failures so the existing provider tracker and candidate fallback can handle them; capture available usage and cost without logging credentials or private prompt content.

Add `openaiBaseUrl` to provider configuration and populate it for mtplx, twilight, and OpenRouter. Keep agentic roles on their existing CLI harnesses and select HTTP only for tool-free triage, chat, and summarize calls when the chosen provider has this endpoint.

Add `limitless local up|down|status`. Manage mtplx on the Mac through its existing launchd service and generate/manage a `llama-server` systemd user unit on twilight through SSH. Make the twilight model path configurable and report each server's service and endpoint health clearly.

Add deterministic tests using a `Bun.serve` OpenAI-compatible fake and injected local/SSH command runners. Update operator documentation for the new URLs, model path, commands, and relationship to `limitless service install`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The HTTP harness accepts valid structured output, extracts and validates JSON from text when needed, makes no more than one corrective retry, and never reports invalid data as a successful structured result.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cancellation, timeout, connection failure, and provider rejection produce bounded failures that allow the existing invocation logic to record the attempt and try an eligible fallback model.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: OpenRouter, mtplx, and twilight expose distinct OpenAI-compatible URLs while agentic calls retain their existing Anthropic-compatible CLI route; missing credentials still make protected providers ineligible.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Extend catalog/router tests to inspect targets for all three providers and assert both tool-free and agentic harness selection; run `bun test test/router.test.ts`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `limitless local up|down|status` starts, stops, and reports both managed servers, generates a twilight user unit containing the configured model path, and handles an unreachable twilight host with a clear partial-status or error report.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add CLI/service tests with injected launchd and SSH runners plus a temporary unit destination; assert generated unit content, commands, idempotent repeated operations, and unreachable-host output.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The new harness and local commands pass repository lint, typecheck, and tests without contacting real models, SSH hosts, or paid services.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun run check`.

out_of_scope: Replacing Claude or Codex CLI for roles that need repository tools.

Downloading models, installing mtplx or llama.cpp, or changing twilight's network security configuration.
Running quota-spending smoke tests as a required gate.

input.prompt:
Graceful deploys

Every `limitless deploy` restarts the daemon, interrupting in-flight runs; they resume at the start
of their current step, but the model work already done in that step is lost.

- Add `POST /api/admin/drain` (localhost only, same CSRF rules as other mutations) and
  `POST /api/admin/resume`: while draining, the scheduler starts no new runs; `/api/health` reports
  `draining: true` and the active run ids.
- `limitless deploy` (after the check/smoke gates pass) drains, waits until no runs are active or
  until `--max-wait` (default 45 minutes) expires, then restarts; `--now` skips waiting. On rollback
  or failure, it resumes the scheduler. Print progress while waiting (active runs and their stages).
- The daemon starts un-drained after a restart. Show a "draining" banner in the UI.
- Tests: drain stops new starts but not active runs; deploy waits and times out correctly (inject a
  fake health client and clock).


Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass. `bun run smoke` exercises the real agent CLIs if you change harness code (optional, spends a little quota).

spec.summary: Add an in-memory drain mode that prevents the scheduler from starting queued runs while allowing active runs to finish. Make deploy wait for those runs after its existing gates pass, with a configurable deadline and an immediate-restart option. Expose drain state through the health API and a live UI banner, and resume scheduling when deployment fails or rolls back.
assumptions: --max-wait accepts non-negative integer seconds, defaults to 2700 seconds (45 minutes), and starts counting after drain is acknowledged. Zero means no waiting; --now takes precedence over a valid --max-wait value.
Both normal deploy and --now request draining; --now skips only the wait, not installation, check gates, optional smoke gates, or post-restart health checks.
Active means membership in Scheduler.activeRunIds, including runs waiting for input or provider capacity while their execution remains active. Queued runs do not extend the wait.
Drain state is process-local and is not persisted. Concurrent deployment coordination and ownership of manually initiated drains are outside this change.

A daemon without the drain endpoint cannot support this graceful deployment path. Missing endpoints or unreadable health data produce an explicit failure rather than silently triggering an immediate restart.
requirements: Extend src/scheduler.ts with idempotent drain/resume operations and readable drain state, initially false. Every scheduling path through tick(), including queue notifications, periodic ticks, and active-run completion, must honor draining before launching another run.

Draining must not abort active controllers, pause active pipelines between stages, or alter run statuses. Continue accepting new and retried runs into the queue and allow existing answer/cancel operations. Resume must promptly reconsider queued work while respecting concurrency limits and the existing stopping guard; preserve stop() shutdown behavior.

Add POST /api/admin/drain and POST /api/admin/resume in src/server/http.ts. Return HTTP 200 JSON containing the resulting draining flag and active run IDs. Repeated calls are harmless, and drain acknowledges after new starts are disabled rather than waiting for active runs to finish.

Restrict both admin endpoints to actual loopback peers, including IPv4, IPv6, and IPv4-mapped loopback addresses. Do not trust Host or forwarded headers as proof of locality. Reuse the existing mutation wrapper: reject Cloudflare-tunnel requests, reject disallowed Origins with 403, and require application/json with 415 otherwise; originless CLI requests remain permitted.

Extend /api/health with an explicit draining boolean while preserving ok, uptimeMs, and active as an array of run IDs. Report scheduler membership rather than inferring activity from persisted run statuses. Share the health response type through src/core/types.ts.

Update src/cli/main.ts argument parsing and help for limitless deploy [ref] [--smoke] [--max-wait <seconds>] [--now]. Reject missing, negative, fractional, non-finite, nonnumeric, or overflowing wait values before deployment side effects, even when --now is supplied.

In src/cli/service.ts, retain the current release selection, installation, check, optional smoke, and same-ref behavior. Only after successful gates, request drain on the local daemon, inspect health immediately, and poll until active is empty or the deadline expires. Keep draining enabled between observing an empty active set and restarting.

Restart immediately when the active set is empty. At the deadline, explicitly report remaining active runs and proceed with the existing restart path; timeout is not itself a deployment failure. --now and --max-wait 0 skip polling delays. Bound HTTP requests and sleeps by the remaining wait budget so an unresponsive request cannot stall the deadline indefinitely.

Print progress immediately and periodically while waiting, including elapsed or remaining time, active run IDs, and their current Run.stage values obtained from existing run-detail responses. Refresh stages during the wait; use an explicit unknown-stage fallback if a run detail disappears or cannot be read. Distinguish completion, timeout, and --now in output.

Preserve deployment rollback behavior and extend cleanup to failures during drain, polling, or restart. If draining may have been enabled, attempt a bounded resume against the surviving or restored daemon before returning failure, including when the drain response was lost. Restore the previous release on failed deployment as appropriate to the existing flow. Preserve the original error and report cleanup failures separately; never interpret failed or malformed health responses as an empty active set.

A restarted or rolled-back daemon must initialize un-drained and retain existing interrupted-run recovery. Successful deployment requires the daemon to become healthy and report draining false; newly started runs after restart are allowed.

Add typed health access and shared reactive drain state in ui/api.ts and ui/store.ts. Render a prominent banner in the shared shell or navigation explaining that active runs continue and new runs are queued. Refresh on initial load, reconnect, and drain/resume changes through bounded polling or the existing SSE architecture, without requiring navigation or reload.

Extend deployment dependency injection beyond the existing command hook to cover admin/health requests, run-detail lookup, clock/sleep, and service restart operations. Add deterministic tests using fake clients and the fake harness, with no real model calls, network requests, gh, launchctl, or production release mutations. Keep strict types and make bun run check pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Draining blocks all new starts while active runs continue through subsequent stages and finish; queued submissions and retries start after resume within the concurrency limit.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add scheduler tests with a controllable fake harness: hold one active run, drain, enqueue another, exercise tick and completion callbacks, and assert no second start or abort. Release the active run, verify continued stage execution, then resume and verify queued execution. Include repeated drain/resume and resume-after-stop checks.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Admin endpoints enforce locality and existing CSRF rules, and health accurately reports drain state and active IDs.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add direct route-handler tests with mocked peer addresses. Verify loopback POST success, idempotency, remote and tunnel rejection, disallowed-Origin 403, missing/non-JSON content-type 415, and no mutation from GET. Assert existing health fields retain their shapes and draining toggles independently of active membership.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A normal deploy drains only after successful gates and restarts only once active runs finish, while displaying their changing stages.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add deployment tests with recorded fake commands and a health sequence containing active runs followed by an empty set. Assert gate-before-drain ordering, no early restart, updated run IDs/stages in progress output, and exactly one successful restart. Cover an initially empty set and unchanged-ref behavior.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The default deadline is 45 minutes; configured deadlines, zero wait, and --now restart as specified without excessive waiting.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use an injected clock and sleep to keep a run active through the deadline. Assert the default is 2700000 milliseconds, shorter deadlines restart at expiry with a timeout message, and zero/--now perform no wait sleeps while retaining gates and drain. Test bounded stalled requests and CLI rejection of invalid wait values before side effects.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Failed deployments do not silently leave an available daemon drained, and rollback preserves scheduling recovery.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Inject failures at gates, drain acknowledgement, health polling, restart, and post-restart health checks. Assert pre-drain gate failure leaves scheduling untouched; subsequent failures attempt resume and appropriate release restoration; unhealthy replacements trigger rollback; cleanup errors remain visible alongside the original failure. Extend the existing smoke-failure regression in test/smoke.test.ts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Drain state disappears across daemon replacement, and interrupted runs retain existing restart recovery behavior.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a lifecycle test that drains one scheduler and constructs a replacement using the same test store. Verify initial draining false, interrupted-run requeue behavior, and eligible work starting without an explicit resume request.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The draining banner appears on every UI route and updates without reload after drain, resume, and restart/reconnect.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use mocked health responses and connection events to exercise initial drained load, false-to-true, true-to-false, and reconnect refresh. Inspect the shared banner on dashboard and run-detail routes and verify its text explains continued active work and queued new work.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All implementation checks pass without invoking real deployment services or paid agents in automated tests.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run bun run check and bun run build:ui. Inspect new test dependencies to confirm health, time, restart, and model execution are faked. Live bun run smoke remains optional and is unnecessary if harness code is unchanged.

out_of_scope: Zero-downtime daemon handover, checkpointing model sessions, or preserving partial model work when a forced restart interrupts a stage.
Changes to harness adapters, provider routing, pipeline stage semantics, or interrupted-run recovery policy.
Persisted drain settings, database migrations, deployment locks, drain leases, or coordination between concurrent deploy processes.
UI controls for drain/resume, public administration endpoints, or new authentication infrastructure.
Redesigning release checkout management, service installation, or unrelated deployment gates.
Repository modifications or test execution as part of this specification-only task.

input.prompt: Add a readingTime utility to textkit: given text and an optional words-per-minute rate (default 200), return the estimated reading time in whole minutes, rounded up, with a minimum of 1 minute for non-empty text and 0 for empty or whitespace-only text. Reject a non-positive or non-finite wpm with a RangeError. Expose it in the CLI as `textkit reading-time [--wpm N] <text>`, update the CLI usage text and the README, and add tests.

spec.summary: Add a `readingTime` function to textkit's text utilities that estimates reading time in whole minutes from word count and an optional words-per-minute rate, wire it into the CLI as a new `reading-time` subcommand, and update documentation and tests to match the existing patterns used by `wordCount`/`truncate`/CLI commands.
assumptions: "Whole minutes, rounded up" means Math.ceil applied to (wordCount / wpm), then clamped to a minimum of 1 only when wordCount > 0 (matches the request's "minimum of 1 minute for non-empty text and 0 for empty or whitespace-only text").
Word counting for readingTime reuses the same whitespace-splitting definition as the existing wordCount function rather than introducing a different tokenizer.

The RangeError message text is not specified by the request; it will follow the existing terse style used by truncate (e.g., "wpm must be a positive, finite number") but exact wording is an implementation detail, not separately tested.

CLI flag parsing for --wpm only needs to support the flag appearing before the text (as shown in the requested usage string `textkit reading-time [--wpm N] <text>`); supporting --wpm after or interspersed within the text is not required.
If --wpm is given a non-numeric or missing value, the CLI will let Number(...) produce NaN, which readingTime already rejects via RangeError — no bespoke CLI error message is required.
README update is a minimal addition (one line/example) consistent with its current brevity, not a full command reference table.
requirements: Add `export function readingTime(text: string, wpm = 200): number` to src/text.ts, placed alongside the other text utilities.
Word count basis: reuse the existing `wordCount(text)` logic (whitespace-trimmed, split on /\s+/) so empty or whitespace-only text yields 0 words.
Minutes calculation: minutes = Math.ceil(wordCount / wpm), except when wordCount > 0 and the ceil result is 0 (i.e., wpm is large relative to word count), clamp up to a minimum of 1.
When wordCount is 0 (empty or whitespace-only text), return 0 regardless of wpm.

Validate `wpm`: if it is not finite (NaN, Infinity, -Infinity) or is <= 0, throw `new RangeError(...)` before computing anything — mirror the style of `truncate`'s `max` validation (`if (max < 1) throw new RangeError("max must be at least 1")`).

Add a `reading-time` subcommand to the CLI (src/cli.ts) with signature `textkit reading-time [--wpm N] <text>`: parse an optional leading `--wpm N` flag (N is the next argv token), then join the remaining args as the text, call `readingTime(text, wpm)`, and print the numeric result via `String(...)`, consistent with how `words` prints `String(wordCount(...))`.

If `--wpm` is passed without a following numeric value, or the value fails `Number()` parsing (NaN), the resulting `Number(...)` NaN must flow into `readingTime` and trigger the existing RangeError validation (no separate CLI-level parsing error handling required).
Update the `USAGE` string in src/cli.ts to document the new command, following the existing two-column alignment style of the other command lines.
Update README.md to mention the new command, consistent with its existing minimal style (it currently shows one example CLI invocation plus lint/typecheck/test commands).

Add unit tests for `readingTime` in test/text.test.ts in a new `describe("readingTime", ...)` block, following the existing test style (using `expect(...).toBe(...)` and `expect(() => ...).toThrow(RangeError)`).
Add a CLI test for the `reading-time` command in the existing `describe("cli", ...)` block, following the pattern of the existing `slugify command` test.
Do not modify unrelated exports (`slugify`, `truncate`, `titleCase`) or their existing tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Default rate: for text with word count N and no wpm argument, readingTime returns Math.max(1, Math.ceil(N/200)) for N > 0.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add/run a test: expect(readingTime("word ".repeat(400).trim())).toBe(2) (400 words / 200wpm = 2min) and expect(readingTime("hello world")).toBe(1) (2 words → ceil(2/200)=0 → clamped to 1).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Empty or whitespace-only text returns 0 regardless of wpm.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: expect(readingTime("")).toBe(0); expect(readingTime("   ")).toBe(0); expect(readingTime("   ", 50)).toBe(0).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Custom wpm is honored and result is rounded up to the next whole minute (not truncated), with the minimum-1 rule applied.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: expect(readingTime("one two three four five", 2)).toBe(3) (5 words / 2wpm = 2.5 → ceil = 3); expect(readingTime("one", 1000)).toBe(1) (1/1000 → ceil=1, confirms min-1 rule holds when already 1).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Non-positive or non-finite wpm values throw RangeError for non-empty text.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: expect(() => readingTime("hello", 0)).toThrow(RangeError); expect(() => readingTime("hello", -5)).toThrow(RangeError); expect(() => readingTime("hello", NaN)).toThrow(RangeError); expect(() => readingTime("hello", Infinity)).toThrow(RangeError).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CLI reading-time command computes reading time using default wpm when no flag is given.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun src/cli.ts reading-time "hello world"` and confirm output is `1`; add equivalent test expect(run(["reading-time", "hello", "world"])).toBe("1").

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CLI reading-time command respects an explicit --wpm N flag placed before the text.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun src/cli.ts reading-time --wpm 2 "one two three four five"` and confirm output is `3`; add equivalent test expect(run(["reading-time", "--wpm", "2", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five"])).toBe("3").

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CLI usage text lists the new reading-time command, and README documents it.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun src/cli.ts` (no args) and confirm the printed usage includes a reading-time line; `grep -n "reading-time" README.md` returns a match.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Full project verification suite passes after the change.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun test` and confirm all pass with zero failures, including the new tests.

out_of_scope: Locale-aware or CJK-aware word/character counting for reading time.
Supporting reading time based on characters instead of words, or configurable rounding modes (floor/nearest).
Adding a general-purpose CLI argument parser/library; keep flag handling minimal and consistent with existing CLI code.
Changing behavior or signatures of existing functions (slugify, wordCount, truncate, titleCase) or their CLI commands.
Publishing/version bump or CHANGELOG entries.

input.prompt: Add a `stats` command to the textkit CLI that reports characters, words, sentences, paragraphs and estimated reading time for the given text. Plain output should be an aligned two-column table; `--json` should print a JSON object instead. Put the counting logic in a reusable `textStats(text)` function in src/text.ts. Sentences end with ., ! or ? (treat runs like '?!' or '...' as one terminator); paragraphs are separated by one or more blank lines. Update the usage text and README, and add tests.

spec.summary: Add a `stats` CLI command that summarizes text in both human-readable and machine-readable formats. The underlying calculations will live in a reusable `textStats(text)` utility, using the repository’s existing word-count and reading-time behavior while adding character, sentence, and paragraph counts. Usage documentation, README examples, and Bun tests will be updated accordingly.
assumptions: `textStats(text)` returns `{ characters, words, sentences, paragraphs, readingTime }`, with every property represented as a number and `readingTime` measured in whole minutes.
Characters are counted using JavaScript string length (`text.length`), including whitespace, punctuation, and line-ending characters.
Word and reading-time calculations reuse the existing `wordCount` and `readingTime` functions; reading time uses the existing default of 200 words per minute and rounds up as currently documented.

A sentence is counted only when it has a terminating run containing `.`, `!`, or `?`; adjacent terminators such as `...`, `?!`, and `!!!` count as one sentence terminator. Unterminated text does not add a sentence.

Paragraphs are non-whitespace text blocks separated by one or more blank lines. Leading/trailing blank lines and multiple consecutive blank lines do not create empty paragraphs; both LF and CRLF input are supported.
Consistent with the existing `reading-time` option parsing, `--json` is recognized immediately after `stats`, as in `textkit stats --json <text>`.
Plain output uses the labels `Characters`, `Words`, `Sentences`, `Paragraphs`, and `Reading time`; reading time is displayed in minutes.
requirements: Export a reusable `textStats(text: string)` function from `src/text.ts`, with an explicit TypeScript-compatible result shape containing numeric `characters`, `words`, `sentences`, `paragraphs`, and `readingTime` fields.
Implement character counting as the input string’s JavaScript length, without trimming or normalizing the input first.

input.prompt:
Retention and cleanup

- Remove worktrees of finished runs after N days (default 3; failed runs 7), prune `git worktree`
  metadata, delete per-run log files after 30 days, and cap the `events` table by deleting debug
  events older than 14 days. Run hourly in the daemon; `limitless gc [--dry-run]` on demand.
- Tests on temp directories and a temp DB.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add retention cleanup for finished-run worktrees, per-run logs, and old debug events so the daemon does not accumulate avoidable disk and database usage. The daemon will run cleanup hourly, and `limitless gc [--dry-run]` will invoke the same cleanup on demand. Cleanup will use the existing run records, repository paths, and Store.
assumptions: Age is measured from `runs.finished_at`, in elapsed 24-hour days. Runs without a terminal status and non-null finish time are ineligible for worktree or log cleanup.
`failed` and `needs_human` runs keep worktrees for 7 days; `succeeded` and `cancelled` runs keep them for 3 days.
The worktree retention period N is configurable in `config.toml`; the other stated periods default to 7, 30, and 14 days.
The CLI invokes cleanup through the local daemon, consistent with the existing CLI pattern, so on-demand cleanup requires a running daemon.
Log cleanup targets invocation `.log` files in known per-run directories. It preserves database artifacts and unrelated files.
requirements: Implement one deterministic cleanup operation shared by the hourly daemon task and the on-demand CLI command; it must make no model, network, or `gh` calls.

Select eligible worktrees from terminal run records using status and `finished_at`, without relying on the current limit of `Store.listRuns` or deleting worktrees for queued, running, or waiting runs.

Remove only the worktree at `paths.work/<run-id>` when it belongs to the run and its registered repository. Use Git worktree removal and prune stale worktree metadata in the relevant repository, including local repositories; handle an already absent worktree idempotently.
Delete per-run invocation log files after 30 days without removing other run files or the run directory. Preserve logs for nonterminal runs.
Delete only `events` rows where `level = 'debug'` and `ts` is older than 14 days; retain newer debug events and all non-debug events.

Make `limitless gc --dry-run` report the worktrees, log files, metadata pruning, and event count it would affect without changing the filesystem, Git metadata, or database. Normal runs report counts and actionable errors.
Run cleanup once when the daemon starts and then hourly, prevent overlapping cleanup passes, and stop its timer during daemon shutdown.
Keep cleanup confined to configured Limitless paths, continue with independent items after a per-item failure, and allow a later pass to retry failed items.
Add focused tests using temporary Git repositories, worktrees, directories, and SQLite databases. Finish implementation with passing `bun run check`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: At the exact retention boundary, finished worktrees become eligible: succeeded and cancelled after 3 days by default, failed and needs_human after 7 days. Younger worktrees remain.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a `bun test` case with a temp DB and temp Git worktrees whose `finished_at` values straddle each boundary; inspect both paths and `git worktree list --porcelain` after cleanup.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Queued, running, and waiting_input worktrees are preserved regardless of age; an eligible run with an already absent worktree does not fail the pass.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a temp DB/worktree test covering each nonterminal status and a missing eligible path, then run `bun test`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cleanup removes eligible per-run invocation logs after 30 days while preserving younger logs, active-run logs, and non-log files.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a temp-directory test with old and young terminal runs, an active run, `.log` files, and an unrelated file; run `bun test` and inspect existence.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Only debug events older than 14 days are deleted, including events belonging to still-active runs.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Seed a temp SQLite DB with debug and non-debug events on both sides of the cutoff; run cleanup and query the remaining event IDs in `bun test`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `limitless gc --dry-run` reports eligible items and counts but leaves worktrees, Git metadata, log files, and events unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Exercise the CLI and daemon endpoint against temporary paths and a temp DB; compare filesystem entries, `git worktree list --porcelain`, and event rows before and after.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Daemon startup and hourly scheduling invoke the same cleanup operation as the CLI, do not overlap passes, and stop scheduling after shutdown.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use an injected cleanup function and controllable timer in a daemon lifecycle test; run `bun test`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A Git or filesystem error on one eligible item is reported while other eligible items are processed, and a later pass can retry it.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a temp-repository failure-injection test with at least two eligible items; run `bun test`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Biome lint, TypeScript typecheck, and the full test suite pass.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run `bun run check`.

out_of_scope: Deleting run records, stages, invocations, questions, database artifacts, or non-debug events.
Deleting branches, bare repository caches, or user-created worktrees outside the configured Limitless work directory.
Database VACUUM, backup rotation, or a general disk-quota system.
