input.prompt:
Add a Discord bot so runs can be started and followed from Discord.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). discord.js is already a dependency and works on Bun. Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

Configuration (already provisioned by the operator):
- Secrets in cfg.secrets: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_APP_ID, DISCORD_GUILD_ID.
- config.toml: `[owners] discord = "<user id>"` (already parsed as cfg.discordOwnerId) and `[discord] channel_id = "<channel id>"` (add parsing in src/config.ts, e.g. cfg.discordChannelId).
- The integration is enabled only when token, app id, guild id and channel id are all present; otherwise startup notes say why it's disabled. It must never crash the daemon (log and keep running if Discord is unreachable; discord.js reconnects on its own).
- Use the gateway connection only. Do not use an HTTP interactions endpoint (nothing may be exposed publicly). Intents: Guilds, GuildMessages, MessageContent.

Behavior:
- New module src/integrations/discord.ts, started from mountIntegrations in src/integrations/index.ts and stopped on shutdown.
- Register guild-scoped slash commands on startup (idempotent): `/build repo:<string> prompt:<string> [profile: auto|quick|standard|deep]`, `/runs [status]`, `/run id:<string>`, `/cancel id:<string>`. Only the owner may use /build and /cancel; everyone else gets an ephemeral refusal. /runs and /run are also owner-only (runs contain repo details).
- /build creates the run through Factory.createRun with source "discord", requestedBy the Discord user id, and sourceRef { kind: "discord", channelId, threadId }. It replies with a short confirmation and creates a public thread in the configured channel named after the run (title, trimmed to Discord's limit), then posts updates into that thread.
- Thread updates (subscribe to store events; only for runs whose sourceRef is a Discord thread): one message per stage transition at most, batched/rate-limited so a run posts no more than ~10 messages total; a message when a question is asked (with the question text); a final message with status, PR link, total cost (real $ and subscription-equivalent) and the UI link (cfg.uiUrl + /runs/<id>). Keep messages concise; use embeds for the final summary.
- Replies in a run thread by the owner answer that run's open questions (Factory.answer with by = "discord:<user id>"). Replies when no question is open get a short hint. Ignore bots and non-owners.
- Optional: when config `[discord] notify_all = true`, also post a one-line notice in the channel when any non-Discord run finishes.
- Keep every Discord API interaction behind a small interface (e.g. DiscordPort with sendMessage/createThread/reply) so the logic is unit-testable with a fake. Tests must not touch the network: command → CreateRunRequest mapping, owner checks, message batching limit, thread reply → answer, disabled-when-unconfigured.
- Document setup and usage in README (bot settings: private bot, Message Content intent, invite via OAuth2 URL generator with scopes bot+applications.commands; commands; thread behavior).

spec.summary: Add an in-process Discord gateway integration so the configured owner can start runs, inspect progress, cancel runs, and answer questions from Discord. Each Discord run gets a thread for concise progress and a final summary, while Discord connection or API failures leave the daemon running.
assumptions: If thread creation fails after a run is created, the run remains valid; the bot reports its ID and UI link and logs the Discord failure.
The approximately 10-message limit applies to routine progress updates. Question messages and the final summary remain deliverable even if a run asks unusually many questions.
A thread reply answers all currently open questions, matching Factory.answer's existing behavior.
The optional notify_all setting defaults to false.
requirements: Add src/integrations/discord.ts and mount it from mountIntegrations; disconnect and unsubscribe through the existing integration stop hook. Use discord.js gateway events with Guilds, GuildMessages, and MessageContent intents. Add no public interactions endpoint.

Parse [discord].channel_id and optional notify_all in src/config.ts. Enable Discord only when DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_APP_ID, DISCORD_GUILD_ID, channel_id, and discordOwnerId are present. Startup notes must identify missing configuration; connection, registration, and messaging errors must be logged without crashing startup or the daemon.

Register the four guild-scoped slash commands idempotently on startup: /build with repo, prompt, and optional auto|quick|standard|deep profile; /runs with optional status; /run with id; and /cancel with id. Reject every non-owner command ephemerally before reading run details or changing state.

Map /build to Factory.createRun with source discord, requestedBy set to the invoking user ID, and sourceRef containing kind discord and the configured channel ID. Confirm the run, create a public thread in the configured channel using its title within Discord's length limit, and persist the resulting thread ID in sourceRef before routing thread updates. The existing source_ref column may be updated through a focused Store method; no schema migration is needed.

Use Store subscriptions for stage, question, and run changes. Route messages only to a Discord run's recorded thread; coalesce repeated stage events, rate-limit routine progress, and reserve delivery for question text and one terminal summary embed. The summary includes terminal status, PR link when present, costUsd, costEquivUsd, and cfg.uiUrl/runs/<id>. Restore routing from persisted sourceRef after a daemon restart.

Accept non-bot messages only from the configured owner in a recorded run thread. Pass their text to Factory.answer with by set to discord:<user id>; when no question is open, give a short hint. Ignore other messages.
Implement /runs, /run, and /cancel through existing Store and Factory APIs, with bounded Discord-length responses and useful unknown-ID, invalid-status, and already-terminal responses.

Put Discord operations behind a small injectable port and add network-free tests using a fake port. Document private bot setup, Message Content intent, OAuth2 URL generator scopes bot and applications.commands, configuration, commands, and thread behavior in README. Run bun run check.

acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Invoke /runs, /run, and /cancel against test Store records; assert responses and cancellation calls with bun test.

input.prompt:
Quota alerts

Tell the operator when a subscription reaches its reserve, so banked resets can be applied in time.

- When a provider transitions into `exhausted` (quota reserve reached, or a hard limit hit), or
  crosses 75% of its reserve for the first time in a window, emit one alert per provider per window:
  a Discord message in the configured channel (when Discord is enabled) and a banner on the UI
  dashboard (a new `alerts` field on `/api/providers` or a small `/api/alerts` endpoint).
- Include the provider, which window, utilization, when it resets, and what the router will do
  meanwhile (which providers it falls back to).
- Tests with a fake Discord port and a fake clock: one alert per window, no alert storms on
  flapping, reset clears it.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add quota alerts so the operator can apply banked resets before a subscription becomes unavailable. The provider tracker will create a durable alert when a quota window first reaches 75% of its configured reserve or the provider becomes exhausted. The dashboard will show the alert, and the existing Discord integration will send it to the configured channel when enabled.
assumptions: 75% of reserve means utilization >= 0.75 × that window’s configured reserve, not 75% of the provider’s hard quota.
The first observation above the threshold counts as a crossing when no earlier observation exists for that window.
A warning and later exhaustion in the same provider window produce one Discord message; the dashboard may update that alert to show the current exhausted state.

Fallback providers depend on routing role and constraints. Alert text will describe that the router skips an exhausted provider and list currently eligible alternatives without promising a universal order.
If a hard limit has no named quota window, use a clearly labeled hard-limit alert and the best available reset estimate; show an unknown reset time when none is available.
requirements: Detect threshold crossings from quota telemetry in ProviderTracker and exhausted transitions caused by either reserve utilization or a quota rejection. Do not treat health failures, circuit breakers, or metered budget exhaustion as subscription quota alerts.

Identify alerts by provider, quota window, and window reset boundary. Persist alert and deduplication state through a new numbered migration so daemon restarts and repeated telemetry cannot resend an alert for the same window.
Rearm a provider-window alert only when that window resets or telemetry identifies a new reset boundary. Expired windows must not keep an alert active.

Expose current alerts through a small /api/alerts endpoint and deliver changes to the dashboard using the existing live update mechanism. Render a visible dashboard banner with provider, window, utilization, reset time, severity, and routing behavior.
When Discord is enabled, send each new alert once to discordChannelId through DiscordPort. Discord being disabled or a send failure must not block quota tracking, routing, or dashboard display.

Build fallback information from current router and provider state. For a warning, say whether the provider remains eligible; for exhaustion, say it is skipped and identify eligible fallback providers or state that none are available.
Keep alert generation deterministic and testable with an injected clock and fake Discord port; do not call paid models, the network, or gh in tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: For each configured subscription window, the first observed utilization at or above 75% of its reserve creates one alert containing the provider, window, utilization, reset time, and routing behavior.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a fake-clock tracker test that observes values below, at, and above 0.75 × the configured reserve, then inspects /api/alerts or the alert store.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Reaching a reserve or receiving a quota rejection creates an exhausted alert even when no earlier warning was observed; health and circuit-breaker transitions do not.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add tracker tests for reserve exhaustion, record(provider, 'quota'), and record(provider, 'unavailable'), asserting the resulting alert set.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Repeated observations, quota-result flapping, and a warning followed by exhaustion send at most one Discord message for the same provider and window, including across a daemon restart.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use the existing fake DiscordPort with a temporary SQLite store; replay those transitions, recreate the tracker and integration, and assert one post to the configured channel.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: After a window resets, its prior alert clears and a threshold crossing in the next window can create a new alert.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Advance the fake clock past resetsAt, inspect /api/alerts, then observe telemetry with a new reset boundary and assert one new alert and Discord post.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The dashboard displays current alerts on initial load and reflects alert creation, exhaustion updates, and clearing without a manual reload.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add an API and live-update test, then inspect the dashboard with seeded provider telemetry and alert transitions.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Alerts identify only currently eligible fallback providers, report when none exist, and remain available in the UI when Discord is disabled or sending fails.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use fake router/provider states and a failing or disabled fake Discord port; assert alert content and continued API availability.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Lint, type checking, and the full test suite pass.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run bun run check.

out_of_scope: Automatically applying banked resets or changing provider quota limits.
Changing routing policy or allowing an LLM to decide alert or fallback behavior.
Adding notification channels other than the existing Discord integration and dashboard.

input.prompt:
GitHub webhook trigger

Add a GitHub webhook integration so runs can be triggered from GitHub.

- New module `src/integrations/github.ts`, mounted from `src/integrations/index.ts` as route
  `POST /webhooks/github`.
- Verify `X-Hub-Signature-256` (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` from
  `cfg.secrets`) using a constant-time comparison; reject with 401 when missing/invalid. If the
  secret is not configured, the route responds 503 and startup notes say webhooks are disabled.
- Deduplicate deliveries by `X-GitHub-Delivery` using `store.recordInbox` (ignore repeats with 200).
  Record every delivery in the inbox with its outcome (`ignored`, `run_created`, `error`) and a note.
- Only act for the owner configured as `cfg.githubOwner` (and `dependabot[bot]` for Dependabot PRs).
  Everything else is recorded as `ignored`. Issue/PR text is untrusted: quote it into the run
  prompt as data, never as instructions.
- Triggers:
  - `issues` with action `labeled` and label `limitless` → run with the issue title + body as the
    prompt, `sourceRef` {kind:"issue", repo, number}.
  - `issue_comment` `created` whose body starts with `/limitless ` by the owner → run with the text
    after the command plus the issue context.
  - `pull_request` `opened`/`reopened`/`synchronize` by `dependabot[bot]` → a `quick` profile run
    whose prompt asks to verify the dependency update (run gates, fix breakages caused by the bump),
    with the run's base branch set to the PR's head branch so the fix lands on Dependabot's branch.
    If that needs engine support (base branch = PR head, deliver by pushing to that branch and
    commenting instead of opening a new PR), add it cleanly.
- Report back on GitHub with the `gh` CLI (factory context, not agents): comment on the
  issue/PR when a run is created (with run id) and when it finishes (status, PR link, cost). Use a
  small notifier that subscribes to store run updates and only reacts to runs with a GitHub
  `sourceRef`.
- Tests: signature verification (valid/invalid/missing), dedupe, owner filtering, each trigger
  mapping to the right CreateRunRequest, and that untrusted text is quoted. Use recorded sample
  payloads; never call GitHub in tests (inject the `gh` runner).
- Document setup in README (webhook URL `https://limitless.mattflower.cc/webhooks/github`, content
  type JSON, secret, events: Issues, Issue comments, Pull requests).

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add an authenticated GitHub webhook that turns selected owner actions and Dependabot pull requests into Limitless runs. Use the existing inbox for delivery deduplication and audit outcomes, and post run updates through a factory-side GitHub notifier. Extend the pipeline’s branch and delivery path so Dependabot fixes can land on the existing pull request.
assumptions: For labeled issues, both the issue author and the actor applying the label must match cfg.githubOwner. For command comments, the commenter must match cfg.githubOwner.
Dependabot runs require a pull request authored by dependabot[bot], an allowed event actor, and a head branch in the same repository as the pull request base.
An authenticated request without X-GitHub-Delivery or with malformed JSON receives 400. Requests that fail authentication are not recorded in the inbox.
Duplicate delivery IDs receive 200 without creating another run or posting another creation comment. A processing failure is recorded as error and reported with a server error.
Comment failures are logged without changing the run outcome.
requirements: Add src/integrations/github.ts and mount POST /webhooks/github through src/integrations/index.ts. Include an enabled or disabled startup note and unsubscribe the notifier during integration shutdown.

When cfg.secrets.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent, return 503. Otherwise verify X-Hub-Signature-256 against an HMAC-SHA256 computed from the unmodified request body bytes, using a constant-time digest comparison; return 401 for missing or invalid signatures.

Atomically claim each authenticated delivery ID with store.recordInbox before creating a run. Extend the store API as needed to finalize the existing inbox row with status ignored, run_created, or error, plus a note and run ID when applicable. Record unsupported events and filtered actors as ignored.

Validate event shape and repository identity before mapping it to CreateRunRequest. Use the payload repository’s canonical full name, source github, and a sourceRef identifying issue or pull request, repository, and number.

Map an owner’s issues.labeled event for the limitless label to a run whose prompt includes the issue title and body. Map an owner’s issue_comment.created event beginning with /limitless followed by text to a run whose prompt includes that text and issue context. Put all issue and comment content in clearly delimited, escaped quoted data sections.

Map pull_request.opened, reopened, and synchronize events for eligible Dependabot pull requests to profile quick. The prompt must ask for dependency update verification, gates, and fixes caused by the bump; quote pull request text as untrusted data.

Extend CreateRunRequest, persistence, prepare, and delivery so a Dependabot run starts from the pull request head branch, works in its own worktree branch, and pushes a verified fast-forward result to that existing head branch. Do not create or merge a new pull request; refuse delivery if the remote head moved or the pull request comes from a fork.

Add a small notifier subscribed to store run events. For GitHub sourceRefs, use an injectable gh runner to comment on the source issue or pull request when a run is created and when it reaches a terminal status. The final comment includes status, any PR link, and cost. Prevent repeated comments from routine updates to the same run state.

Add recorded sample payload tests for authentication, deduplication, filtering, trigger mapping, quoted untrusted text, inbox outcomes, notifier behavior, and Dependabot branch delivery. Tests must use fakes for paid models and gh and make no network calls. Document the webhook URL, JSON content type, secret, and Issues, Issue comments, and Pull requests events in README.

input.prompt:
Quota alerts

Tell the operator when a subscription reaches its reserve, so banked resets can be applied in time.

- When a provider transitions into `exhausted` (quota reserve reached, or a hard limit hit), or
  crosses 75% of its reserve for the first time in a window, emit one alert per provider per window:
  a Discord message in the configured channel (when Discord is enabled) and a banner on the UI
  dashboard (a new `alerts` field on `/api/providers` or a small `/api/alerts` endpoint).
- Include the provider, which window, utilization, when it resets, and what the router will do
  meanwhile (which providers it falls back to).
- Tests with a fake Discord port and a fake clock: one alert per window, no alert storms on
  flapping, reset clears it.

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass.

spec.summary: Add quota alerts so the operator can apply banked resets before a subscription becomes unavailable. The provider tracker will create a durable alert when a quota window first reaches 75% of its configured reserve or the provider becomes exhausted. The dashboard will show the alert, and the existing Discord integration will send it to the configured channel when enabled.
assumptions: 75% of reserve means utilization >= 0.75 × that window’s configured reserve, not 75% of the provider’s hard quota.
The first observation above the threshold counts as a crossing when no earlier observation exists for that window.
A warning and later exhaustion in the same provider window produce one Discord message; the dashboard may update that alert to show the current exhausted state.

Fallback providers depend on routing role and constraints. Alert text will describe that the router skips an exhausted provider and list currently eligible alternatives without promising a universal order.
If a hard limit has no named quota window, use a clearly labeled hard-limit alert and the best available reset estimate; show an unknown reset time when none is available.
requirements: Detect threshold crossings from quota telemetry in ProviderTracker and exhausted transitions caused by either reserve utilization or a quota rejection. Do not treat health failures, circuit breakers, or metered budget exhaustion as subscription quota alerts.

Identify alerts by provider, quota window, and window reset boundary. Persist alert and deduplication state through a new numbered migration so daemon restarts and repeated telemetry cannot resend an alert for the same window.
Rearm a provider-window alert only when that window resets or telemetry identifies a new reset boundary. Expired windows must not keep an alert active.

Expose current alerts through a small /api/alerts endpoint and deliver changes to the dashboard using the existing live update mechanism. Render a visible dashboard banner with provider, window, utilization, reset time, severity, and routing behavior.
When Discord is enabled, send each new alert once to discordChannelId through DiscordPort. Discord being disabled or a send failure must not block quota tracking, routing, or dashboard display.

Build fallback information from current router and provider state. For a warning, say whether the provider remains eligible; for exhaustion, say it is skipped and identify eligible fallback providers or state that none are available.
Keep alert generation deterministic and testable with an injected clock and fake Discord port; do not call paid models, the network, or gh in tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: For each configured subscription window, the first observed utilization at or above 75% of its reserve creates one alert containing the provider, window, utilization, reset time, and routing behavior.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a fake-clock tracker test that observes values below, at, and above 0.75 × the configured reserve, then inspects /api/alerts or the alert store.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Reaching a reserve or receiving a quota rejection creates an exhausted alert even when no earlier warning was observed; health and circuit-breaker transitions do not.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add tracker tests for reserve exhaustion, record(provider, 'quota'), and record(provider, 'unavailable'), asserting the resulting alert set.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Repeated observations, quota-result flapping, and a warning followed by exhaustion send at most one Discord message for the same provider and window, including across a daemon restart.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use the existing fake DiscordPort with a temporary SQLite store; replay those transitions, recreate the tracker and integration, and assert one post to the configured channel.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: After a window resets, its prior alert clears and a threshold crossing in the next window can create a new alert.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Advance the fake clock past resetsAt, inspect /api/alerts, then observe telemetry with a new reset boundary and assert one new alert and Discord post.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The dashboard displays current alerts on initial load and reflects alert creation, exhaustion updates, and clearing without a manual reload.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add an API and live-update test, then inspect the dashboard with seeded provider telemetry and alert transitions.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Alerts identify only currently eligible fallback providers, report when none exist, and remain available in the UI when Discord is disabled or sending fails.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Use fake router/provider states and a failing or disabled fake Discord port; assert alert content and continued API availability.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Lint, type checking, and the full test suite pass.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run bun run check.

out_of_scope: Automatically applying banked resets or changing provider quota limits.
Changing routing policy or allowing an LLM to decide alert or fallback behavior.
Adding notification channels other than the existing Discord integration and dashboard.

Rebase before delivery

When the base branch moved while a run was working, deliver should rebase instead of opening a PR
that conflicts.

- In `deliver`, fetch the base branch; if it advanced past `run.baseSha`, rebase the run branch onto
  it. On a clean rebase, re-run the gates (not review/verify) and only deliver if nothing regressed;
  update `baseSha`.
- On conflicts: abort the rebase and run one extra implement round whose feedback tells the agent to
  merge the new base (`git merge origin/<base>`), resolve conflicts preserving both intents, and
  re-run checks; then continue through gates/audit/review as usual.
- Tests with local git repos: base advanced without conflict (rebased, gates re-run), with conflict
  (extra round), base unchanged (no-op).

Context: this is the Limitless repository itself (see AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Keep changes consistent with the existing architecture and code style, and make `bun run check` pass. `bun run smoke` exercises the real agent CLIs if you change harness code (optional, spends a little quota).

spec.summary: Before delivering a new GitHub branch, Limitless will fetch its base branch and check whether it advanced since the run’s recorded `baseSha`. A clean rebase will trigger another gate run before delivery; a conflicting rebase will be aborted and sent through one additional implement round with merge-resolution feedback. This prevents delivery of a branch known to conflict with its base.
assumptions: This applies to new GitHub PR delivery. Existing PR-head updates keep their current webhook-head and guarded-push behavior.
Tests use local bare Git repositories as remotes, the fake harness, and no network or `gh` calls.
A gate regression after a clean rebase blocks delivery; it does not trigger another review or verify.
requirements: At successful delivery, fetch the configured base branch and compare its fetched tip with `run.baseSha`. If unchanged, continue the existing delivery path.
If the fetched tip descends from `run.baseSha`, rebase the committed run branch onto that exact tip. Do not publish while a rebase is in progress.

After a clean rebase, rerun the configured setup and gates, persist their results, and block delivery if a previously passing check now fails or setup prevents checks from running. Do not rerun audit, review, or verify solely because the rebase was clean.
After successful post-rebase gates, persist the new `baseSha` and rebased `headSha` before building the delivery report and publishing.

If rebase conflicts, abort it and verify the worktree is out of rebase state. Give the implementer one additional round, even if the normal round budget was exhausted, with feedback directing it to merge `origin/<base>`, resolve conflicts while preserving both intents, and rerun checks.
Run the conflict-resolution round through the existing gates, diff audit, and review flow, plus verify where the run profile requires it. Use the new base SHA for subsequent diffs and delivery.

Persist enough phase and round state for a restart to resume the appropriate post-rebase gate check or conflict-resolution round without publishing an unchecked branch. If the base changes again before publication, fail closed or repeat the base check.

# Free-first routing for Dependabot runs ($0 on local models)

## Why
The M4 exit criterion (docs/PLAN.md, docs/EVALS.md) is a Dependabot PR handled end-to-end on local models for $0. Today a Dependabot run (`quick` profile: triage → implement → gates → audit → review → deliver to the PR branch) routes through the normal policy: implement goes to `claude/haiku|codex/luna` or Sonnet/Sol, review to Sol/Sonnet, triage to OpenRouter. The local providers (`mtplx`, `twilight`, billing `free`) are never tried for implement/review.

## Design
- `RouteConstraints` gains `billing?: "free_first"`. With it, `Router.decideRoute` orders candidates as: free-billing models first, then everything else in normal policy order.
  - Free candidates = free-billing models named in the role's policy list (keeping their policy order and effort), then any other free catalog model at its catalog default effort. Existing filters still apply (disabled/unhealthy provider, excluded, effort transport, minTier).
  - Vendor avoidance still applies inside each billing class: free cross-vendor, free same-vendor, then paid cross-vendor, paid same-vendor.
- Config: `[routing] dependabot = "free_first"` (default) or `"policy"`, parsed in `src/config.ts` next to `routing.prefer`.
- Engine: for runs with `requestedBy === "dependabot[bot]"` and the setting `free_first`, every `ctx.invoke` in that run passes `billing: "free_first"` (triage, implement, review, summarize). No new persisted fields; no migration.
- The report states the routing mode for such runs (one line, e.g. "Routing: free-first (Dependabot)").

## Acceptance
- Fake-harness tests: a Dependabot run with a free provider available uses free models for triage, implement and review; with free providers disabled or unhealthy it falls back to the normal policy and still completes; an owner run with the same config is unaffected.
- Router unit tests for the ordering above (policy-named free models first, catalog free models next, vendor partition inside each class).
- `bun run check` passes.

## Out of scope
- Changing `routing/policy.json` or `DEFAULT_POLICY`.
- New eval work. Keep the change under ~300 lines.

Closes #42

spec.summary: Add a free-first routing mode for Dependabot runs so available local models are tried for triage, implementation, review, and any summary invocation. When local models are unavailable or ineligible, the run falls back to the existing policy so it can still complete. The report will identify the routing mode; a $0 result depends on every invocation using a free provider.
assumptions: Only runs whose requestedBy value is exactly "dependabot[bot]" use this mode, regardless of source or profile.
When routing.dependabot is omitted, its value is "free_first". The "policy" value preserves current routing.
A free model is identified by its provider's billing value, not by a zero price in the model catalog.

The requested vendor order takes precedence over policy-list versus catalog-list order: free cross-vendor, free same-vendor, paid cross-vendor, then paid same-vendor. Existing order is retained within each partition.
An existing implementer preference cannot move a paid candidate ahead of an eligible free candidate in free-first mode.
requirements: Add billing?: "free_first" to RouteConstraints. With no billing constraint, Router.route must retain its current candidate ordering and behavior.

For free-first routing, consider free models named in the selected role and complexity policy entry in policy order and at their policy-specified effort, followed by other free catalog models at their catalog default effort. Then consider non-free candidates in normal policy order.

Apply existing exclusions, disabled or unhealthy provider checks, model availability, effort transport checks, and minTier to every candidate. Preserve vendor avoidance within each billing class and preserve existing fallback behavior when no free candidate is eligible.
Parse [routing] dependabot = "free_first" or "policy" in src/config.ts beside routing.prefer, defaulting to "free_first".

For a run requested by "dependabot[bot]" with free-first enabled, pass the billing constraint on every RunContext.invoke call, including calls with existing constraints such as review vendor avoidance and implementation escalation. Keep the pipeline deterministic and add no persisted field or migration.
Show a single routing-mode line in the generated report for free-first Dependabot runs.
Use fake-harness tests and focused router tests; do not call real models, network services, or gh. Keep the implementation under roughly 300 changed lines.

# Conflict-free migrations for parallel branches

## Why
`src/db/migrations.ts` is one array with sequential `version` integers. Two parallel runs that each add a migration both append `version: N+1` at the end of the same array, so every such pair conflicts, and the orchestrator has renumbered by hand several times (v5–v12).

## Design
- One file per new migration: `src/db/migrations/<UTC timestamp>-<slug>.sql`, e.g. `20260927T1500-run-dependencies.sql`. Files load at startup (`readdirSync`, sorted by filename) and are applied in order inside a transaction each.
- Track applied migrations by name in a `schema_migrations(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER)` table. On first start after this change, record the existing array migrations 1..N (named `legacy-0001-<name>`...) as applied according to the current `user_version`. The legacy array stays frozen and append-only rules move to the directory.

# Deploy: finish or roll back an interrupted deploy

## Why
A deploy killed while draining (SIGTERM/SIGINT) left the release checkout at the new commit, already installed and checked, and the daemon still on the old code in `draining` state. Queued runs were then blocked indefinitely. Re-running `deploy` printed `already at <sha>` and returned, because it compares the target to the checkout rather than to the running daemon.

## Design
- `/api/health` reports the commit the daemon booted from (`sha`, read once at startup).
- `deploy` compares the target to the running daemon's `sha`, not the checkout. If the checkout already matches the target but the daemon runs another commit, continue from "gates passed": drain, wait, restart. If the daemon is draining and nothing is deploying, say so and resume it or continue.
- Install SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers for the duration of a deploy. Before the restart, roll back the checkout and resume the scheduler, then exit non-zero. After the restart, just exit.
- `deploy` prints the daemon `sha` before and after.

## Acceptance
- Tests with the injectable `command`/`client`/`restart`:
  - checkout at target with the daemon on the previous sha → drains and restarts;
  - both at target → "already deployed", no restart;
  - a signal during the drain wait → checkout restored and resume requested;
  - health includes `sha`.
- `bun run check` passes; under ~200 lines.

Closes #51

spec.summary: Make deployment decisions from the commit running in the daemon, so an interrupted deploy can finish even when the release checkout already contains the target. Expose the daemon’s boot commit in health, recover a stranded drain, and handle deploy signals so interruption before restart restores service.
assumptions: When the checkout already matches the target but the daemon runs an older commit, the prior install and checks completed; deploy resumes at draining.
The running daemon’s SHA is the rollback commit, even if the checkout has already moved.
A draining daemon at the target commit has no deploy to finish, so deploy resumes its scheduler.
A daemon that cannot provide a valid boot SHA cannot be used for automatic interrupted-deploy recovery.
requirements: Read the daemon’s commit once at startup and expose it as sha in /api/health and HealthResponse; changing the checkout must not change that value in the running process.

Compare the resolved target with the daemon SHA before deciding that deployment is complete. When checkout and target match but daemon and target differ, skip checkout, install, and gates, then drain, wait, and restart.
If the daemon is already draining, report that state and either continue a pending deployment or request resume when the target is already running.

During deploy, handle SIGINT and SIGTERM and remove the handlers afterward. A signal before restart must restore and reinstall the daemon’s commit, request scheduler resume, and cause a nonzero exit. A signal after restart begins must exit without restoring the old checkout or resuming the old daemon.
Print the daemon SHA before deployment and the healthy replacement daemon SHA afterward; do not report success if the replacement runs a different commit.
Keep the change focused, around 200 lines, and preserve the existing injectable command, client, clock, and restart test seams.

acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add and run a focused health route test in test/drain-http.test.ts using an injected boot SHA and a changed checkout.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: With checkout at target and daemon on the previous SHA, deploy skips install and gates, drains, waits, restarts once, and reports both daemon SHAs.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add an injected command/client/restart test in test/deploy.test.ts and assert calls, ordering, and logs; run bun test test/deploy.test.ts.

acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add tests for both draining states in test/deploy.test.ts; assert no restart and a resume call only for the draining case.

acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a test starting with health.draining true, checkout at target, and daemon SHA at previous; assert drain completion and one restart.

Changing scheduler behavior outside deploy recovery.
Changing release delivery, pushing commits, or opening pull requests.

# Implement evals part A: runner, case format, hidden-test grader

Part A of #41. Adds an `implement` role to the eval framework (`src/evals/`), so implement routing can be backed by evidence like triage. Single round only; multi-round and escalation are part B.

## Case format: `evals/implement/cases.json`
`{ role: "implement", version: 1, notes?, cases: [...] }`. Each case:
- `id`, `repo` (owner/name), `base` (full pinned SHA the task starts from), `head` (reference-solution SHA, provenance only, never fetched into a trial)
- `complexity`: `trivial | small | medium`
- `prompt`: the task as the requester would write it
- `spec`: a `SpecSchema` object or `null` (null = quick-profile style, prompt only)
- `hidden`: `{ files: string[], command: string, timeoutSec?: number }`. `files` are repo-relative paths whose contents live at `evals/implement/hidden/<case-id>/<path>`; `command` runs them (e.g. `bun test test/strip.test.ts`)
- `source` (where the task came from), `tags`, `notes?`
Validate with zod like the other case files: unique ids; hidden files exist in the dataset dir and don't escape it (see `seedContent`).

## Trial
Trials run in the existing standalone trial repo pinned at `base` (only the pinned history; see `prepare.ts` / isolation).
1. Detect gates as of `base` (`gatesAt`) and run the baseline gates. The baseline may be cached per case.
2. Invoke the candidate in write mode through the real harness, using `implementPrompt({ prompt, spec, gates, baseline, baseSha: base, round: 0, feedback: undefined, hasHoldout: false })`, the same builder the pipeline uses.
3. Commit the result, compare gates (`compareGates`) and audit the diff (`auditDiff`, as the pipeline does).
4. Only now copy the hidden files into the trial repo (overwriting same-named paths) and run `hidden.command` with the scrubbed agent env and a timeout. Hidden output is never shown to the model.
5. Grade: `pass` = hidden command exit 0 AND no blocking gate AND no blocking audit finding. Record pass, the reason for failure (`hidden_tests | gates | audit | error | timeout`), gate verdicts, audit blocks, hidden-output tail, actual and subscription-equivalent cost, tokens, and wall time.
- The cache key includes the case (base, prompt, spec, hidden-file hashes) plus model, effort, harness and prompt hash.
- Extend the label-exposure check so hidden-file contents count as labels.

## Reporting
`limitless eval run implement --models ... [--k N] [--cases ...]` and `eval report` show pass rate with Wilson CI overall and by complexity, failure reasons, median wall time and cost per trial. The UI evals matrix should render implement results with no new UI work beyond what the role list needs.

## Tests (fake harness only)
- A passing trial, one failing on hidden tests, and one failing on gates.
- Hidden files are absent from the repo while the implementer runs.
- The cache key changes when a hidden file changes.
- Case-file validation errors.

## Out of scope
Multi-round feedback, escalation strategies and policy-generator changes (part B), and the dataset itself (authored separately). Keep the change under ~800 lines.

Closes nothing on its own; tracked by #41.

Closes #43

spec.summary: Add single-round implementation evaluations to the existing eval framework so candidate models can be measured against hidden tests, repository gates, and deterministic diff audits. Reuse the production implement prompt, harness selection, isolated repositories, persistence, and reporting to produce comparable evidence without exposing reference solutions or hidden tests to candidates.
assumptions: Use mode="edit", the existing harness API’s write mode. Pass feedback=null because implementPrompt currently accepts string | null; this represents the requested absence of feedback.
Default hidden.timeoutSec to 900 seconds, matching repository gate execution. Explicit values must be finite and positive.
When multiple failures occur, select one primary reason in this order: timeout, error, gates, audit, hidden_tests. Preserve all available grading evidence.
Hidden contents must remain absent during implementation. A same-named file already present at base remains available with its original contents and is overwritten only during hidden grading.

Report cost per trial as the arithmetic mean for actual and subscription-equivalent costs. Report wall time as the median elapsed execution time from baseline preparation through grading, excluding provider queue waits and cache hits.

The UI matrix currently receives policy-derived data. Minimal role and presentation plumbing is permitted, but implement evidence must not introduce new routing recommendations or policy eligibility rules.
requirements: Add implement to eval role types, request validation, dataset loading, runner dispatch, and reporting. Replace structural checks such as `"prompt" in item` wherever they would misclassify implement cases as triage. Preserve existing triage, review, and verify behavior.

Define a strict version-1 implement case envelope with optional notes and a nonempty cases array. Each case contains unique id, owner/name repo, full 40-character base and head SHAs, complexity (trivial|small|medium), nonblank prompt, required SpecSchema-or-null spec, hidden configuration, source, tags, and optional notes.

Resolve hidden files relative to the loaded dataset’s directory at hidden/<case-id>/<path>. Before scheduling trials, validate file existence and regular-file status, safe case IDs and repository-relative paths, and realpath containment as in seedContent. Reject traversal, absolute paths, NULs, and symlink escapes. Recheck destination containment when injecting files so candidate-created symlinks cannot redirect writes outside the trial repository.

Prepare each trial in an independent standalone repository containing only history reachable from base. Do not resolve, require, fetch, import, or check out the reference head for implement trials; retain it solely as provenance. Preserve source repositories and clean up trial resources on success, failure, timeout, and cancellation.

Extend label exposure checks with evals/implement and hidden-file contents from the dataset, including detection of identical contents under unrelated filenames or in reachable historical commits. Perform these checks before candidate invocation and retain existing isolation safeguards.

Detect gate configuration with gatesAt(base), run baseline gates, and construct implementPrompt with the case prompt/spec, pinned gate configuration, baseline, baseSha=base, round=0, absent feedback, and hasHoldout=false. Baseline caching is optional and must not mix cases or pins or omit setup needed by a fresh trial.

Invoke the requested model and resolved effort exactly once through the selected harness in edit mode, using the existing factory preamble, scratch handling, budget, provider tracking, and cancellation facilities. Accept the normal free-text implementation report without requiring a structured-output schema. Do not perform retries, feedback rounds, or escalation.

Commit candidate changes, run post-change gates using the base gate configuration, discard gate-generated changes as the pipeline does, and use compareGates. Audit the candidate diff against base with auditDiff, including pinned protected paths, before/after gate scripts, and captured tool commands. Use taskClass=null because implement cases provide no task class.

Only after candidate invocation, commit, gate comparison, and audit have finished, copy the validated hidden contents into the trial repository, overwriting same-named files. Execute hidden.command through /bin/sh in that repository with agentEnv and bounded process execution. Do not include hidden files in the candidate commit or audit, or expose hidden contents, commands, output, or grading feedback to the model.

A normally completed trial passes exactly when the hidden command succeeds without timeout, no gate comparison is blocking, and no audit finding is blocking. Operational errors and timeouts fail the trial. Persist pass, binary score, complexity, primary failure reason, gate verdicts, blocking audit findings, hidden exit/timeout information and bounded output tail, implementation report, actual and equivalent cost, tokens, and wall time. Preserve existing skipped/interrupted lifecycle semantics.

Extend the canonical cache identity with repo/source identity, base, prompt, spec, hidden paths and content hashes, hidden command and timeout, candidate model, resolved effort, harness, rendered prompt/preamble identity, and repetition index. Cache complete grading evidence rather than attempting to regrade an implementation report as structured model output. Preserve source usage metadata and existing zero-additional-spend cache accounting.

Support limitless eval run implement --models ... with existing --k, --cases, budget, cache, and follow behavior, plus eval report in text and JSON. For each model/effort, report overall and per-complexity pass counts, rates and 95% Wilson intervals, failure-reason counts, median wall time, and actual/equivalent cost per executed trial. Exclude queued/skipped trials from pass denominators, include completed errors as failures, and show unavailable values for empty groups.

Expose implement results through the existing UI matrix and report views using minimal role/presentation plumbing. Keep policy-generation behavior unchanged. Use strict types and append-only migrations for any required persisted-schema changes; target approximately 800 changed lines and reuse existing helpers.

acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Extend test/evals-cli.test.ts, test/evals-http.test.ts, and test/evals-page.test.ts using fake/local fixtures. The changed files are lint-clean, so the three warnings belong to files I didn't touch. All checks pass.

## Report

**Finding fixed:** the baseline Git cleanup in `src/evals/implement.ts` now runs with the scrubbed agent environment. Baseline gates execute repository code before that cleanup and can install a clean filter via `.git/config` and `.gitattributes`. Previously the cleanup's `git status` ran that filter with the daemon environment, leaking daemon secrets. Now both `discardChanges` calls in the implement trial use `agentEnv()`, with a comment explaining why the post-baseline checkout is untrusted.

**Files changed**
- `src/evals/implement.ts`: pass `agentEnv()` to the baseline `discardChanges` call.
- `test/evals-implement-runner.test.ts`: the fixture accepts extra files committed at `base`. New regression test commits a baseline gate script that installs a leaking clean filter, marks a tracked file with it, and dirties that file. It asserts, inside the fake harness callback and after the trial, that the filter ran but captured an empty secret, the dirtied file was restored, the candidate was invoked once, and the trial passed.

**Verification**
- Reverted the fix temporarily and ran the new test in isolation: it fails, so it genuinely reproduces the leak. Restored the fix and confirmed the file is back to the fixed state.
- `bun test test/evals-implement-runner.test.ts`: 15 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run check`: lint exit 0, typecheck exit 0, 441 tests pass across 55 files. The lint warnings reported are in untouched files. Biome on the two changed files reports nothing.

**Assumptions and scope**
- Only the reviewed finding was addressed. The pipeline engine has its own unscrubbed `discardChanges` calls, but those are outside this task and the review comment, so I left them alone.
- Nothing was committed or pushed.

input.prompt:
# UI changes can be verified in a real browser

## Why
UI runs can't pass verification today. On the owner's first UI run (#52, 2026-09-27), the criteria that needed a browser (collapse toggle, rendered line counts, no horizontal scroll at phone width) were reported `blocked` in every round:
- Headless Chrome won't start inside the agent sandbox: it writes under `~/Library` and needs its own nested sandbox.
- The `agent-browser` CLI's daemon failed to start for the same reason.
- `npm` installs are blocked by the network policy.
The orchestrator then verified by hand: build the UI, serve it on a spare port with a throwaway home seeded with test runs, and drive a browser at desktop and 375px widths. This issue automates exactly that.

## Design (the browser runs outside the agent sandbox; the pipeline, not the model, controls it)
1. **Preview service (pipeline).** For runs whose diff touches the repo's declared UI paths, a deterministic `preview` step before verify:
   - builds and starts the app on an ephemeral loopback port with a scrubbed env (`agentEnv`, like gates) and a throwaway home in the run's scratch area;
   - runs an optional seed script;
   - waits for a readiness URL, and stops it after verify.
   The repo declares this in `.limitless.toml`:
   ```toml
   [preview]
   paths = ["ui/"]
   build = "bun run build:ui"
   serve = "bun src/cli/main.ts serve"
   env = { LIMITLESS_HOME = "{scratch}/home", LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR = "{scratch}/config", LIMITLESS_PORT = "{port}" }
   seed = "bun scripts/preview-seed.ts"   # e.g. runs with long, short and whitespace-only prompts
   ready = "/api/health"
   ```
   Limitless ships its own `[preview]` and seed script.
2. **Browser for the verifier (harness).** When a preview is running, the verify invocation (and implement, for UI work) gets a Playwright MCP server (`@playwright/mcp`, pinned, installed once into the factory's tool cache; no network installs at run time).
   - MCP servers are spawned by the `claude`/`codex` CLI outside the agent's command sandbox and talk over stdio, so Chrome starts normally.
   - Launch it headless and isolated, with its user-data/output dirs in the run scratch area and an origin allowlist of just the preview URL.
   - Check the pinned version's exact flags. Both adapters already pass per-invocation config, so extend them.
3. **Prompts and evidence.**
   - The verify prompt gets a "Browser" section: the preview URL, the viewports to check (desktop and 375px), and the rule that visual/interactive criteria must be checked in it, with the evidence citing what was observed.
   - Screenshots the verifier takes are saved as run artifacts (`screenshot-*.png`), and the report links them.
   - `blocked` stays valid only if the preview itself fails to start; that is a pipeline error, reported as such.
4. **Spec guidance** (unchanged from before): state UI criteria so most are checkable with component/SSR tests, and keep the visual checks as a short explicit list.

## Acceptance
- Tests with fakes:
  - the preview step starts, serves and tears down a tiny fixture app, and fails cleanly on build error or readiness timeout;
  - verify invocations for UI-touching runs include the MCP config with the allowlist, and non-UI runs don't;
  - screenshot artifacts are stored.
- Live check by the orchestrator: a small UI change goes through verify with no `blocked` criteria.
- Two runs of under ~800 lines each: (1) preview service, config and the Limitless seed script; (2) MCP wiring for both adapters, prompt and artifacts.

SCOPE FOR THIS RUN: part (1) only: the preview service, the [preview] config in .limitless.toml, and Limitless's own [preview] section and seed script. Do NOT wire the browser/MCP yet (that is a separate run). Refs #33 (do not close it).

spec.summary: Add a deterministic preview step for runs whose committed diff touches UI paths declared in the repository’s `.limitless.toml`. It will build and seed a private Limitless instance, serve it on an ephemeral loopback port, wait for readiness, and keep it running through verification. This gives the later browser wiring a reliable preview URL without requiring browser work in this run.
assumptions: The preview runs only when the pipeline reaches verify; quick profile runs have no verify stage.
The seed command runs after a successful build and before the server starts.
A preview startup failure fails the pipeline step with a clear error; it is not recorded as a blocked acceptance criterion.
requirements: Parse an optional `[preview]` section from the worktree’s `.limitless.toml` with `paths`, `build`, `serve`, `env`, optional `seed`, and `ready`. Validate required values and report malformed configuration clearly.

Select preview using the committed diff already produced by `diffSince`, matching declared directory prefixes against both source and destination paths for renamed files. Repositories without preview configuration, and diffs outside its paths, skip the step.

Run build and seed commands in the worktree with `agentEnv`, a private scratch directory, and expanded `{scratch}` and `{port}` values. Bind the server to `127.0.0.1` on an available ephemeral port; apply the same scrubbed environment and configured variables to serving.
Use bounded build, seed, and readiness waits. Treat command failure, premature server exit, and readiness timeout as distinct preview errors with useful bounded output.

Keep the server alive across the verify invocation and its retry, then stop its process tree and remove scratch data on success, failure, or cancellation. Record preview as a pipeline stage before verify.

Add Limitless’s own `[preview]` configuration for `ui/`, `bun run build:ui`, `bun src/cli/main.ts serve`, and `/api/health`. Add a small seed script that creates representative long, short, and whitespace-only prompt runs only in the throwaway `LIMITLESS_HOME`; set `LIMITLESS_NO_SCHEDULER=1` for the preview server so seeded data cannot launch paid runs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A UI path change with valid preview configuration builds, seeds, serves, reaches the configured readiness URL, and exposes its loopback URL while verify runs.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add a focused pipeline test using a tiny local fixture app and fake harness; assert the health endpoint responds during verify and the seeded fixture data is available.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No preview process starts when `[preview]` is absent or the diff touches no declared UI path; renamed files are selected when either old or new path matches.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add selection tests covering absent config, a non-UI diff, a UI edit, and renames into and out of `ui/`; run them with `bun test`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A failed build or seed command fails preview before verify starts, and a server that exits early or misses its readiness deadline fails with a diagnostic error.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add fixture tests for each failure mode and assert no fake verify invocation occurs and the reported error identifies the failed step.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Preview and its scratch directory are cleaned up after successful verify, a verify retry, verify failure, and cancellation.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Add lifecycle tests that check the port no longer responds and the scratch path no longer exists after each outcome.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Limitless’s checked-in preview configuration and seed script produce representative runs in the throwaway data directory without starting the scheduler or touching the operator’s normal data directory.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: Run the seed script with temporary `LIMITLESS_HOME` and `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR`, inspect the resulting SQLite runs for long, short, and whitespace-only prompts, and use a fixture or focused test to assert the serve environment contains `LIMITLESS_NO_SCHEDULER=1`.

out_of_scope: Playwright MCP installation or wiring in either harness adapter.
Browser instructions in implement or verify prompts, screenshots, artifact links, and report changes.
Changing verifier verdict semantics or performing the orchestrator’s live browser check.
Closing issue #33.

# Implement evals part B1: multi-round trials and escalation strategies

Part B1 of #41, building on the implement runner from #56. Question: when the cheap tier fails a task, is it better to (a) retry the same model, (b) raise effort on the same model and keep its session, or (c) switch to a stronger model in a fresh session? Today the pipeline does (c). The needs-human analysis suggested that (b) may converge better, because switching loses context.

## Design
- `eval run implement ... --rounds N` (default 1, which is today's behaviour) and `--strategy retry|effort|switch` (default `retry`).
  - Round 0 is the candidate as given.
  - If round 0 fails on gates, audit or hidden tests, round r ≥ 1 continues according to the strategy:
    - `retry`: same model and effort, same session (resume) where the harness supports it.
    - `effort`: same model at the next supported effort level (`low → medium → high`), same session.
    - `switch`: the next tier from the implement policy for the case's complexity (e.g. luna → sol → astra), in a fresh session.
- **Feedback between rounds** mirrors the pipeline: the formatted gate and audit feedback (the same formatter the engine uses), plus for hidden-test failures only a count ("N acceptance tests fail"). Never test names, output or content, so hidden tests stay hidden.
- **Recorded per trial:** rounds used, the model and effort per round, pass at each round, and cost/time per round. The cache key includes the rounds and the strategy.
- **Report:** pass@1 and pass@R per candidate and strategy, and for trials that failed round 0, the recovery rate per strategy with a Wilson CI and cost per recovery.

## Acceptance
- Fake-harness tests:
  - a failing-then-passing trial under each strategy calls the expected model, effort and session sequence;
  - hidden-test output never appears in any round's prompt (assert on captured prompts);
  - `--rounds 1` is byte-identical to today's trial, so cache keys don't change;
  - the report aggregates recovery rates.
- `bun run check` passes; under ~600 lines.

Closes #67

spec.summary: Extend implement evals with bounded multi-round trials comparing same-model retries, effort escalation with session reuse, and stronger-model escalation with fresh sessions. Record each round and report first-attempt success, eventual success, recovery rates, and recovery costs while preserving hidden-test confidentiality and existing single-round cache compatibility.
assumptions: N is the maximum total number of invocations per trial, including round 0; --k continues to control independent trials.

Stop early when no strategy-compliant escalation exists, recording the reason instead of silently changing strategies. Effort escalation uses supported levels within low → medium → high; an explicit none may advance to low. An unresolved backend-default effort, high/xhigh, or unsupported effort transport cannot escalate.

Switch means a strictly higher catalog tier present in the effective implement policy for the case complexity, using existing provider preference and availability rules among alternatives. It need not retain the original provider.

Both session-preserving and fresh-session strategies retain previous implementation changes. When session resumption is unavailable or no session ID is returned, retry/effort may start a fresh session with the same worktree and sanitized feedback.

The current hidden-test interface provides one command and its exit status, not individual assertion counts. Treat a nonzero command exit as one failed acceptance-test unit and send only '1 acceptance tests fail'; do not infer counts from arbitrary output or introduce a new test-results protocol.

Cost per recovery means incremental spend after round 0 across all executed trials that initially failed grading, divided by the number recovered among those trials. Include unsuccessful recovery attempts in spend; exclude cache hits from both cost numerator and recovery denominator.

Single-round byte compatibility applies to deterministic invocation inputs, grading behavior, and cache-key material, excluding inherently variable IDs, timestamps, durations, and additive report metadata.

# Deploy drain parks runs at the next stage boundary

## Why
`Scheduler.drain()` stops starting new runs and the deploy then waits for every active run to finish (up to `--max-wait`, default 45 min). A single long run blocks both the deploy and every queued run. Runs already persist state per stage and resume after a restart, so a deploy only needs the current stage to finish.

## Design
- While draining, the engine checks the drain flag at each stage boundary (before starting the next stage, at the same points it checks cancellation). If set, it parks the run: persist state, set status back to `queued` (or a `parked` sub-status if the UI needs to tell them apart), and release the scheduler slot without running `deliver` or cleanup.
- `/api/health` reports `active` (a stage is mid-flight) separately from `parked`. The deploy waits only until nothing is active.
- After restart, parked runs resume from their persisted phase through the normal queue, in priority/creation order.
- A stage that is mid-flight when `--max-wait` expires is handled exactly as today (it replays after restart).

## Acceptance
- Fake-harness test: a run mid-implement when drain is requested finishes implement, parks before gates, and resumes at gates after a simulated restart with the same round and state.
- Queued runs don't start while draining. A parked run keeps its worktree.
- A deploy with three active runs completes after the longest *current stage*, not the longest run.
- `bun run check` passes; under ~400 lines.

Closes #44

spec.summary: Change deploy drain so each running pipeline finishes its current stage and parks before starting the next one. The scheduler can then release its slots, and deploy can restart once no stages are active instead of waiting for entire runs. Parked runs will resume from their persisted state through the normal queue.
assumptions: Use the existing queued run status plus a persisted parked marker in run state, avoiding a new database status and migration.
A stage already in progress is allowed to finish; if it exceeds --max-wait, the existing restart and replay behavior applies.
Cancellation takes precedence over parking when both are requested at a boundary.

At a drain boundary, atomically retain the current phase and round state, mark the run queued and parked, clear its active stage, and return from execution without delivery, cleanup, or terminal status.
Keep the worktree and completed stage records. Resume must skip an already completed implementation in the same round using the existing implementedRound checkpoint.
Do not start queued or parked runs while draining. After restart or resume, dispatch them through nextQueuedRuns, which orders by priority descending and creation time ascending.
Report active run IDs and parked run IDs separately from /api/health. The deploy wait ends when active is empty, regardless of parked count.
Preserve existing cancellation, stage failure, --now, and --max-wait behavior. Keep the implementation approximately under 400 added lines.
